tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

content.text:
<system-reminder>
Codebase and user instructions are shown below. Be sure to adhere to these instructions. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.

Contents of c:\Users\Aarushi\Downloads\LaunchWitness\CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

# CLAUDE.md — LaunchWitness

Read this file fully at the start of every session. It is the source of truth for how you work in this repo.

## What we are building

LaunchWitness (working name) — GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026, Round 2 (build Nov 13–20, 2026).

> Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy and proves everything works before your first customer arrives.

A small seller types a few lines + a price list. LaunchWitness builds her site from one fixed template, buys/points her domain, sets up her email, then **proves** it all works (HTTPS, DNS, email records, a real test order arriving in her inbox), repairs or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps lightly checking afterwards.

Full product spec: `docs/SPEC.md`. Milestones and acceptance criteria: `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`.

## Session ritual (every session, no exceptions)

1. **Start:** read `CLAUDE.md`, then `docs/PROGRESS.md` (current milestone, what's done, what's next, open questions). Only read `docs/SPEC.md` / `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` sections relevant to today's task.
2. **Before coding:** state in 3–6 bullets what you will do this session and which acceptance criteria from `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` it targets. Wait for the user's OK if the plan changes anything in `docs/SPEC.md`.
3. **While coding:** small commits, each one working. Run tests before every commit.

- learning-framework:active-recall: Active Recall (Retrieval Practice) — The testing effect by Roediger·Karpicke. Retrieval (re-test) beats re-study for long-term memory. Pitfalls of highlighting·rereading, the generation effect, desirable difficulty.
- learning-framework:chunking: Chunking — Miller's 7±2 short-term memory constraint, expert chunk perception, and chunk-size calibration in learning design. Meaningless individual items → meaningful chunks = expanded processing capacity. The core representational unit of expertise.
- learning-framework:deep-work: Deep Work — Cal Newport. Distinguishing shallow work from deep work, attention as a muscle, and the four disciplines (monastic/bimodal/rhythmic/journalistic). A framework for designing focused time blocks for knowledge workers.
- learning-framework:deliberate-practice: Deliberate Practice — Anders Ericsson's theory of deliberate practice. Expertise is forged not by time but by *conditions*: specific goals, immediate feedback, just beyond current limits, intense focus. The '10,000-hour rule' is Gladwell-style hyperbole that Ericsson himself refuted.
- learning-framework:evergreen-notes: Evergreen Notes — Andy Matuschak's digital note-taking practice. Concept-oriented, continuously edited, densely linked, atomic. A digital successor to Zettelkasten and more than research notes. Notes are not disposable but *something you come back to and revise*.
- learning-framework:feynman-technique: Feynman Technique — a method of revealing gaps in understanding by explaining to a beginner. 4-step protocol (Choose → Teach → Identify gaps → Simplify). ELI5 approach. The fastest tool to break the illusion of competence.
- learning-framework:interleaving: Interleaving — mixing multiple topics and problem types during study. Compared to blocked repetition, short-term performance ↓ but long-term retention and transfer ↑. Bjork's desirable difficulty. Effectiveness demonstrated in math problem types, sports skills, and language training.
- learning-framework:metalearning: Metalearning — Barbara Oakley *Learning How to Learn* + Scott Young *Ultralearning*. Focused/diffuse modes, illusion of competence, MOC (map of content), learning project design. The upper layer for rapidly acquiring new fields.
- learning-framework:pomodoro-and-focus: Pomodoro Technique (Cirillo 25/5) + focus variants (50/10, 90-minute ultradian). Sophie Leroy's attention residue. Train attention muscle through short focus units + timeboxing tool. The implementation layer of Deep Work.
- learning-framework:second-brain-para: Building a Second Brain — Tiago Forte's personal knowledge management system. PARA (Projects/Areas/Resources/Archives) organization + CODE (Capture/Organize/Distill/Express) workflow. Strong on execution-orientation and project linkage. For when you're drowning in information or stuck on where to put what.
- learning-framework:spaced-repetition: Spaced Repetition — interval-based review learning rooted in Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve. SM-2 and FSRS algorithms. Anki and SuperMemo lineage. The strongest tool for memorizing terminology, facts, language vocabulary, medicine, and law. Managing the long-term retention curve.
- learning-framework:zettelkasten: Zettelkasten — Niklas Luhmann's atomic-note, link-based knowledge system. Distinguishes fleeting/literature/permanent notes, one note = one idea, connections matter more than content. For long-term knowledge accumulation, writing, and researchers.

1	# LaunchWitness — Final Build Spec
2	
3	As of 2026-11-14 · GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026 (HackerEarth) · Round 2 build Nov 13–20 · submit by Nov 20 · Top 10 announced Nov 30 · onsite finale Pune, Dec 11.
4	
5	LaunchWitness is a working name.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Pitch
10	
11	**One line for judges:** "Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy and proves everything works before your first customer arrives."
12	
13	LaunchWitness takes a small seller from a few lines of description to a live business on her own domain: website, business email, and an order form that reaches her inbox. Then it checks every part for real, fixes or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps checking lightly afterwards.
14	
15	**What makes it different.** Most AI builders stop at "your site is ready." LaunchWitness shows the proof: a real test order arriving in her inbox, every check green, and a report with the time each one passed. The safety rules (approve before spending, preview before changing, undo on failure) are what let an AI be trusted to spend money and change settings for a non-technical owner.
16	
17	**Why it fits GoDaddy.** Small businesses buying a domain, a website and an email is GoDaddy's core business. LaunchWitness uses GoDaddy's Domains, DNS and Email as the engine, not decoration. GoDaddy's own AI tools already help people get online; LaunchWitness adds the missing piece: proof that it all works, before customers find out it doesn't.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. Problem and the story
22	
23	Small sellers either never get their own online presence, or they get one that is quietly broken.
24	
25	1. **They don't start, because setup is technical.** A GoDaddy survey found 63% of India's small businesses had no website; of those planning one, only 15% owned a domain, and 30% wanted someone to build and manage it for them (DNA India). The survey is several years old: present it as background, not today's figure.
26	2. **When they do start, it's often half-working.** A March 2026 analysis put DMARC adoption at 44.9% for small businesses vs 75.3% for large enterprises (Cross-Sector DNS & Email Security). A scan of 200 small and mid-size business domains found 36% missing SPF and over two-thirds with no DMARC record (DEV). Result: order emails land in spam, and the owner never knows — she just thinks business is slow.
27	3. **AI could do the setup, but isn't trusted to.** Buying a domain and changing settings means spending money and risking email. An owner who can't read a DNS record can't check an agent's work.
28	
29	Open question: find one current (2025–26) India-specific figure on small businesses without websites before the deck.
30	
31	**Demo persona: Meera.** Meera sells custom cakes from home and takes orders over Instagram DMs. No website, no business email, never touched DNS. She types two lines and pastes her price list. A few minutes later she has meerabakes.in with her real menu and prices, hello@meerabakes.in, and an order form that lands in that inbox. Before she shares the link with a single customer, LaunchWitness places a test order, watches it arrive, and shows her: **"Your business is ready for customers."**
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 3. How it works (user flow)
36	
37	Seven steps from description to proof; Meera does four of them, and only one costs money.
38	
39	1. **Describe.** A few lines + price list (typed, pasted or photo). No WhatsApp/Instagram API.
40	   - Claude (one call) returns the business profile (name, products, prices, hours, area, tone) **plus** the site copy (tagline, about, item descriptions) **plus** how customers order: selling point, days of notice, pickup / delivery and delivery charge, whether customers may add a message for an item, the name the seller's UPI app shows, and her food licence (FSSAI) number if given. Plain code then tidies the reply (delivery is never a menu item; extras such as toppers are marked as extras; ordering rules leave the hours line).
41	   - **Scope guard (v1 = sellers who take orders).** If the business needs bookings rather than orders (salon, tuition, clinic, classes), the Reader says so in one plain sentence and no shop is built.
42	2. **Review.** She sees the profile as a form and fixes anything wrong. No AI.
43	3. **Pick a name.** Claude (one small call) suggests ~10 domain names; code checks real availability + price; shows the best 3.
44	4. **Preview and approve.** Code fills the ONE fixed template, the same for every seller (no per-business code or CSS; category colours come from a fixed palette by position): header with short badges taken only from her data, menu with prices and an Add button per item (a basket that also works without JavaScript; long menus get two columns and a search box), extras listed apart, about, hours, pickup/delivery, "Order on WhatsApp" link (`wa.me`), UPI QR with "Your UPI app should show: <name>", optional FSSAI number in the footer, privacy page. No "Verified" label anywhere. One approval card lists the domain, total cost and every setting to be made. **Nothing is bought or changed until she taps Approve.**
45	5. **Launch.** Code only: back up DNS, buy the domain (or use a free sandbox subdomain), point it at the server, set up email, put the site live with HTTPS. Each step streams on screen.
46	6. **Launch check.** Code checks the site opens, HTTPS is valid, email settings are correct, then places a real test order through her form. If anything fails, the Doctor explains it in one sentence, applies a safe fix or undoes the change, and re-checks until green.
47	7. **Report and watch.** Report headed **"Your business is ready for customers"**: every check, result, time passed. After launch, the same checks re-run lightly on a timer and alert her if something breaks.
48	
49	**Two launch modes, same code:**
50	- **Sandbox launch** at `<slug>.<APP_DOMAIN>`: free, real DNS writes on the app's own domain, real checks. Used for development, rehearsals and judges trying it.
51	- **Full launch** on a purchased domain: run once, for the recorded demo.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 4. Features
56	
57	Eight core features first; no stretch item starts until all eight run end to end.
58	
59	| # | Feature | Tier | What it does |
60	|---|---|---|---|
61	| 1 | Business reader | Core | Description + price list (text or photo) → editable profile + site copy, one Claude call |
62	| 2 | Name finder | Core | Claude suggests names; code checks real availability and price; shows 3 |
63	| 3 | Site builder | Core | One fixed template for every seller: badges from data, menu + basket, extras, about, hours, pickup/delivery, order form, WhatsApp link, UPI QR, privacy page |
64	| 3a | Orders and payment (session 9) | Core | Order date (min notice enforced), pickup/delivery, quantities, totals worked out on the server; per-order UPI pay link + QR (no gateway, no money passes through us); order ID + status page (Received → Confirmed → Paid → Preparing → Ready / Out for delivery → Delivered / Picked up, or Cancelled); seller's order list on her private link; WhatsApp hand-offs via `wa.me` links |
65	| 3b | Trust and safety (session 9) | Core | Verify the owner's email before any real launch; Claude policy check that can only hold a shop for team review (never launches); "Report this shop" link + admin pause switch |
66	| 4 | Launch engine | Core | Plan → preview of changes → approval card → execute (GoDaddy Domains, DNS, Email); sandbox + full modes |
67	| 5 | Launch check | Core | Site resolves, HTTPS valid, email settings present, real test order arrives |
68	| 6 | Repair during launch | Core | Doctor explains a failed check, applies a playbook fix or undoes from backup, re-checks |
69	| 7 | Launch report | Core | One page per business: every check, result, timestamp, plus audit log |
70	| 8 | Light monitoring | Core (light) | Timer re-checks, domain/cert expiry warnings, alert to personal email, "Run checks now" |
71	| 9 | Full monitoring | Stretch | Daily test order, change detection ("Was this you?"), incident history |
72	| 10 | /verify page | Stretch | Official Instagram/WhatsApp listed, backed by a DNS TXT record, so buyers spot fakes |
73	| 11 | MCP server | Stretch | Engine tools over MCP behind the same safety gates |
74	| 12 | Fleet view | Stretch | Dashboard of all launched businesses |
75	
76	Out of scope: payment gateways or holding money (UPI pay links only; "Connect Razorpay (after seller KYC)" is future work), appointments/booking, inventory, SMS, WhatsApp Business / Instagram APIs, multiple templates, custom code generation.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## 5. Agents
81	
82	Claude decides and explains; plain code acts and checks. Three steps use Claude; nothing that spends money or changes settings is left to the model alone.
83	
84	| Agent | Job | Claude or code | Model | Output |
85	|---|---|---|---|---|
86	| Reader | Profile + site copy + ordering details from text or photo; orders vs bookings | Claude, 1 call | Strong (vision + structured output) | Profile JSON + copy (code tidies it) |
87	| Policy check (session 9) | Is this shop OK to put live? | Claude decides, code holds | Cheap | OK, or "hold for review" + one plain reason; it can never launch or unpause |
88	| Namer | Suggest names; check availability + price | Claude suggests, code checks | Cheap | 3 available domains with prices |
89	| Planner | Every action, setting and cost | Code, fixed schema | — | Plan + before/after preview |
90	| Executor | Run the approved plan step by step, backup first | Code only | — | Step log |
91	| Checker | Live checks | Code only | — | Pass/fail per check |
92	| Doctor | Explain a failed check in one sentence; pick a fix | Claude chooses, code applies | Cheap | Fix + re-check result |
93	
94	A manager loop runs them in order and stops at the approval card. **Doctor playbook (fixed, in code):** undo from backup · re-add MX · re-add SPF/DKIM/DMARC · retry certificate · re-point site address. It cannot write arbitrary settings.
95	
96	Cost shape: ~3 Claude calls per launch + 1 per failed check.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 6. Launch checks and repair
101	
102	Repair happens during launch, because that's where setups actually go wrong: settings not spread yet, a certificate failing first time, a mailbox not ready, an email setting missing, a step failing halfway.
103	
104	| Check | How | If it fails |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| Domain points to the site | DNS lookup against GoDaddy's authoritative nameservers (not a cached resolver) | Re-point, wait, re-check |
107	| Site opens over HTTPS | Fetch, validate certificate | Retry certificate, re-check |
108	| Email settings correct | Look up MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Re-add the missing record from the plan |
109	| Test order arrives | Submit the real form; email carries a "Yes, I got it" link | Check mailbox readiness + MX, retry |
110	| Launch finished cleanly | Step log shows every step done | Resume the failed step, or undo DNS from backup |
111	
112	**Repair rules:** max 3 attempts per check, then stop and explain in plain words. Repair never spends money. Every attempt goes to the audit log.
113	
114	**Confirming the test order:** for real sellers the app can't read their inbox (GoDaddy emails mailbox passwords to the account owner only), so the seller taps "Yes, I got it". For the demo mailbox, the checker can also read the inbox over IMAP (password in env).
115	
116	**Demo failure:** during launch one check fails on purpose (e.g. DMARC missing → orders would land in spam). The Doctor explains, re-adds, re-checks to green. The fault is staged — say so if asked.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 7. Monitoring after launch
121	
122	Light monitoring is core; full only if time permits. It re-runs launch checks on a timer (GoDaddy's API has no webhooks).
123	
124	**Light (build now)**
125	
126	| How often | What |
127	|---|---|
128	| Every 15 minutes | Site opens, HTTPS valid |
129	| Daily | DNS + email settings still match launch; days left on certificate and domain |
130	
131	- On failure: re-check once a minute later (rule out blips), then Doctor explains + safe playbook fix.
132	- Anything needing money or her action (renewal, payment): alert only, at 30 / 7 / 1 days before expiry.
133	- Alerts go to her **personal email**, not the business inbox.
134	- "Run checks now" button = same checks on demand (this is how the demo shows it).
135	
136	**Full (if time permits):** daily real test order; change detection ("Was this you? Tap to restore") instead of silent undo; incident history on the report.
137	
138	**Honest framing:** in the demo everything sits in the app's GoDaddy account, so little can break after launch. Monitoring matters most once it runs on her own account. Pitch it as insurance, not the hero.
139

142	## 8. Architecture and GoDaddy usage
143	
144	One GoDaddy Docker VPS (4 vCPU / 8 GB, provided at $0) runs everything; GoDaddy and Claude are called as APIs.
145	
146	- **Caddy:** HTTPS for the app and every seller site; on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint that only approves domains in the DB.
147	- **FastAPI:** agents, API, monitoring scheduler, and every seller site (served by `Host` header from one template + profile).
148	- **React (Vite):** seller-facing app, built and served as static files.
149	- **SQLite:** profiles, plans, DNS backups, check results, audit log.
150	- **Outside:** Claude API; GoDaddy Domains/DNS/Email (OTE sandbox in dev, `GODADDY_ENV=ote|prod`); SMTP through the app's one mailbox.
151	- **Secrets** live only in environment variables.
152	- **Sandbox subdomains** need a wildcard `*.<APP_DOMAIN>` A record → VPS.
153	
154	| Step | GoDaddy piece | Calls |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| Name | Domains API (or `gddy`) | availability, suggestions, price quote |
157	| Buy | godaddy.com checkout with credit (demo); Domains API purchase only behind guards | purchase after approval |
158	| Point | DNS API | list records (backup), set A, MX, SPF/DKIM/DMARC |
159	| Mailbox | Titan email via `gddy` / Email API | create mailbox, poll until ready |
160	| Host | Docker VPS | A record → VPS; Caddy issues HTTPS |
161	| Undo | DNS API | write backup back |
162	
163	**Access limits:** production Availability API needs 50+ domains or ~$20/month spend; DNS API needs ≥1 domain. So: buy the app domain first; check availability via `gddy`, OTE, or free RDAP if production stays blocked.

# LaunchWitness — Final Build Spec

As of 2026-11-14 · GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026 (HackerEarth) · Round 2 build Nov 13–20 · submit by Nov 20 · Top 10 announced Nov 30 · onsite finale Pune, Dec 11.

LaunchWitness is a working name.

---

## 1. Pitch

**One line for judges:** "Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy and proves everything works before your first customer arrives."

LaunchWitness takes a small seller from a few lines of description to a live business on her own domain: website, business email, and an order form that reaches her inbox. Then it checks every part for real, fixes or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps checking lightly afterwards.

**What makes it different.** Most AI builders stop at "your site is ready." LaunchWitness shows the proof: a real test order arriving in her inbox, every check green, and a report with the time each one passed. The safety rules (approve before spending, preview before changing, undo on failure) are what let an AI be trusted to spend money and change settings for a non-technical owner.

**Why it fits GoDaddy.** Small businesses buying a domain, a website and an email is GoDaddy's core business. LaunchWitness uses GoDaddy's Domains, DNS and Email as the engine, not decoration. GoDaddy's own AI tools already help people get online; LaunchWitness adds the missing piece: proof that it all works, before customers find out it doesn't.

---

## 2. Problem and the story

Small sellers either never get their own online presence, or they get one that is quietly broken.

1. **They don't start, because setup is technical.** A GoDaddy survey found 63% of India's small businesses had no website; of those planning one, only 15% owned a domain, and 30% wanted someone to build and manage it for them (DNA India). The survey is several years old: present it as background, not today's figure.
2. **When they do start, it's often half-working.** A March 2026 analysis put DMARC adoption at 44.9% for small businesses vs 75.3% for large enterprises (Cross-Sector DNS & Email Security). A scan of 200 small and mid-size business domains found 36% missing SPF and over two-thirds with no DMARC record (DEV). Result: order emails land in spam, and the owner never knows — she just thinks business is slow.
3. **AI could do the setup, but isn't trusted to.** Buying a domain and changing settings means spending money and risking email. An owner who can't read a DNS record can't check an agent's work.

Open question: find one current (2025–26) India-specific figure on small businesses without websites before the deck.

**Demo persona: Meera.** Meera sells custom cakes from home and takes orders over Instagram DMs. No website, no business email, never touched DNS. She types two lines and pastes her price list. A few minutes later she has meerabakes.in with her real menu and prices, hello@meerabakes.in, and an order form that lands in that inbox. Before she shares the link with a single customer, LaunchWitness places a test order, watches it arrive, and shows her: **"Your business is ready for customers."**

---

## 3. How it works (user flow)

Seven steps from description to proof; Meera does four of them, and only one costs money.

1. **Describe.** A few lines + price list (typed, pasted or photo). No WhatsApp/Instagram API.
   - Claude (one call) returns the business profile (name, products, prices, hours, area, tone) **plus** the site copy (tagline, about, item descriptions) **plus** how customers order: selling point, days of notice, pickup / delivery and delivery charge, whether customers may add a message for an item, the name the seller's UPI app shows, and her food licence (FSSAI) number if given. Plain code then tidies the reply (delivery is never a menu item; extras such as toppers are marked as extras; ordering rules leave the hours line).
   - **Scope guard (v1 = sellers who take orders).** If the business needs bookings rather than orders (salon, tuition, clinic, classes), the Reader says so in one plain sentence and no shop is built.
2. **Review.** She sees the profile as a form and fixes anything wrong. No AI.
3. **Pick a name.** Claude (one small call) suggests ~10 domain names; code checks real availability + price; shows the best 3.
4. **Preview and approve.** Code fills the ONE fixed template, the same for every seller (no per-business code or CSS; category colours come from a fixed palette by position): header with short badges taken only from her data, menu with prices and an Add button per item (a basket that also works without JavaScript; long menus get two columns and a search box), extras listed apart, about, hours, pickup/delivery, "Order on WhatsApp" link (`wa.me`), UPI QR with "Your UPI app should show: <name>", optional FSSAI number in the footer, privacy page. No "Verified" label anywhere. One approval card lists the domain, total cost and every setting to be made. **Nothing is bought or changed until she taps Approve.**
5. **Launch.** Code only: back up DNS, buy the domain (or use a free sandbox subdomain), point it at the server, set up email, put the site live with HTTPS. Each step streams on screen.
6. **Launch check.** Code checks the site opens, HTTPS is valid, email settings are correct, then places a real test order through her form. If anything fails, the Doctor explains it in one sentence, applies a safe fix or undoes the change, and re-checks until green.
7. **Report and watch.** Report headed **"Your business is ready for customers"**: every check, result, time passed. After launch, the same checks re-run lightly on a timer and alert her if something breaks.

**Two launch modes, same code:**
- **Sandbox launch** at `<slug>.<APP_DOMAIN>`: free, real DNS writes on the app's own domain, real checks. Used for development, rehearsals and judges trying it.
- **Full launch** on a purchased domain: run once, for the recorded demo.

---

## 4. Features

Eight core features first; no stretch item starts until all eight run end to end.

| # | Feature | Tier | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Business reader | Core | Description + price list (text or photo) → editable profile + site copy, one Claude call |
| 2 | Name finder | Core | Claude suggests names; code checks real availability and price; shows 3 |
| 3 | Site builder | Core | One fixed template for every seller: badges from data, menu + basket, extras, about, hours, pickup/delivery, order form, WhatsApp link, UPI QR, privacy page |
| 3a | Orders and payment (session 9) | Core | Order date (min notice enforced), pickup/delivery, quantities, totals worked out on the server; per-order UPI pay link + QR (no gateway, no money passes through us); order ID + status page (Received → Confirmed → Paid → Preparing → Ready / Out for delivery → Delivered / Picked up, or Cancelled); seller's order list on her private link; WhatsApp hand-offs via `wa.me` links |
| 3b | Trust and safety (session 9) | Core | Verify the owner's email before any real launch; Claude policy check that can only hold a shop for team review (never launches); "Report this shop" link + admin pause switch |
| 4 | Launch engine | Core | Plan → preview of changes → approval card → execute (GoDaddy Domains, DNS, Email); sandbox + full modes |
| 5 | Launch check | Core | Site resolves, HTTPS valid, email settings present, real test order arrives |
| 6 | Repair during launch | Core | Doctor explains a failed check, applies a playbook fix or undoes from backup, re-checks |
| 7 | Launch report | Core | One page per business: every check, result, timestamp, plus audit log |
| 8 | Light monitoring | Core (light) | Timer re-checks, domain/cert expiry warnings, alert to personal email, "Run checks now" |
| 9 | Full monitoring | Stretch | Daily test order, change detection ("Was this you?"), incident history |
| 10 | /verify page | Stretch | Official Instagram/WhatsApp listed, backed by a DNS TXT record, so buyers spot fakes |
| 11 | MCP server | Stretch | Engine tools over MCP behind the same safety gates |
| 12 | Fleet view | Stretch | Dashboard of all launched businesses |

Out of scope: payment gateways or holding money (UPI pay links only; "Connect Razorpay (after seller KYC)" is future work), appointments/booking, inventory, SMS, WhatsApp Business / Instagram APIs, multiple templates, custom code generation.

---

## 5. Agents

Claude decides and explains; plain code acts and checks. Three steps use Claude; nothing that spends money or changes settings is left to the model alone.

| Agent | Job | Claude or code | Model | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reader | Profile + site copy + ordering details from text or photo; orders vs bookings | Claude, 1 call | Strong (vision + structured output) | Profile JSON + copy (code tidies it) |
| Policy check (session 9) | Is this shop OK to put live? | Claude decides, code holds | Cheap | OK, or "hold for review" + one plain reason; it can never launch or unpause |
| Namer | Suggest names; check availability + price | Claude suggests, code checks | Cheap | 3 available domains with prices |
| Planner | Every action, setting and cost | Code, fixed schema | — | Plan + before/after preview |
| Executor | Run the approved plan step by step, backup first | Code only | — | Step log |
| Checker | Live checks | Code only | — | Pass/fail per check |
| Doctor | Explain a failed check in one sentence; pick a fix | Claude chooses, code applies | Cheap | Fix + re-check result |

A manager loop runs them in order and stops at the approval card. **Doctor playbook (fixed, in code):** undo from backup · re-add MX · re-add SPF/DKIM/DMARC · retry certificate · re-point site address. It cannot write arbitrary settings.

Cost shape: ~3 Claude calls per launch + 1 per failed check.

---

## 6. Launch checks and repair

Repair happens during launch, because that's where setups actually go wrong: settings not spread yet, a certificate failing first time, a mailbox not ready, an email setting missing, a step failing halfway.

| Check | How | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Domain points to the site | DNS lookup against GoDaddy's authoritative nameservers (not a cached resolver) | Re-point, wait, re-check |
| Site opens over HTTPS | Fetch, validate certificate | Retry certificate, re-check |
| Email settings correct | Look up MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Re-add the missing record from the plan |
| Test order arrives | Submit the real form; email carries a "Yes, I got it" link | Check mailbox readiness + MX, retry |
| Launch finished cleanly | Step log shows every step done | Resume the failed step, or undo DNS from backup |

**Repair rules:** max 3 attempts per check, then stop and explain in plain words. Repair never spends money. Every attempt goes to the audit log.

**Confirming the test order:** for real sellers the app can't read their inbox (GoDaddy emails mailbox passwords to the account owner only), so the seller taps "Yes, I got it". For the demo mailbox, the checker can also read the inbox over IMAP (password in env).

**Demo failure:** during launch one check fails on purpose (e.g. DMARC missing → orders would land in spam). The Doctor explains, re-adds, re-checks to green. The fault is staged — say so if asked.

---

## 7. Monitoring after launch

Light monitoring is core; full only if time permits. It re-runs launch checks on a timer (GoDaddy's API has no webhooks).

**Light (build now)**

| How often | What |
|---|---|
| Every 15 minutes | Site opens, HTTPS valid |
| Daily | DNS + email settings still match launch; days left on certificate and domain |

- On failure: re-check once a minute later (rule out blips), then Doctor explains + safe playbook fix.
- Anything needing money or her action (renewal, payment): alert only, at 30 / 7 / 1 days before expiry.
- Alerts go to her **personal email**, not the business inbox.
- "Run checks now" button = same checks on demand (this is how the demo shows it).

**Full (if time permits):** daily real test order; change detection ("Was this you? Tap to restore") instead of silent undo; incident history on the report.

**Honest framing:** in the demo everything sits in the app's GoDaddy account, so little can break after launch. Monitoring matters most once it runs on her own account. Pitch it as insurance, not the hero.

---

## 8. Architecture and GoDaddy usage

One GoDaddy Docker VPS (4 vCPU / 8 GB, provided at $0) runs everything; GoDaddy and Claude are called as APIs.

- **Caddy:** HTTPS for the app and every seller site; on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint that only approves domains in the DB.
- **FastAPI:** agents, API, monitoring scheduler, and every seller site (served by `Host` header from one template + profile).
- **React (Vite):** seller-facing app, built and served as static files.
- **SQLite:** profiles, plans, DNS backups, check results, audit log.
- **Outside:** Claude API; GoDaddy Domains/DNS/Email (OTE sandbox in dev, `GODADDY_ENV=ote|prod`); SMTP through the app's one mailbox.
- **Secrets** live only in environment variables.
- **Sandbox subdomains** need a wildcard `*.<APP_DOMAIN>` A record → VPS.

| Step | GoDaddy piece | Calls |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Domains API (or `gddy`) | availability, suggestions, price quote |
| Buy | godaddy.com checkout with credit (demo); Domains API purchase only behind guards | purchase after approval |
| Point | DNS API | list records (backup), set A, MX, SPF/DKIM/DMARC |
| Mailbox | Titan email via `gddy` / Email API | create mailbox, poll until ready |
| Host | Docker VPS | A record → VPS; Caddy issues HTTPS |
| Undo | DNS API | write backup back |

**Access limits:** production Availability API needs 50+ domains or ~$20/month spend; DNS API needs ≥1 domain. So: buy the app domain first; check availability via `gddy`, OTE, or free RDAP if production stays blocked.

Say plainly to judges: hosting is the Docker VPS, not GoDaddy's Hosting API.

---

## 9. Safety rules

1. **Approve before spending.** Purchase/mailbox only after Approve on a card showing exact cost.
2. **Preview before changing.** Every DNS change shown as a before/after diff first.
3. **Back up, then undo.** Before any DNS write, save current records as JSON. Failed launch check can write the backup back. Failed mailbox step is retried, not undone.
4. **Scoped actions.** Each launch touches only its own domain. Doctor picks from a fixed playbook; anything else is refused and logged.
5. **Spend guards in code.** `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false` default, hard `MAX_SPEND_USD` cap, purchase only when flag on AND owner approved.

Every step goes to the audit log shown in the report.

---

## 10. Budget

**GoDaddy:** VPS is added to the cart at $0 by organizers. ~$25 in-store credit covers domain + email. Buy on godaddy.com only after organizers confirm credit; use the CLI to explore and manage.

| Item | Paid by | Expected cost | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 vCPU / 8 GB Docker VPS | Organizers ($0 in cart) | $0 | Check out after confirmation |
| App domain | Credit | Cart price; compare with `gddy` | Buy first (unlocks DNS) |
| Titan Pro Light, 1-month term, 1 mailbox | Credit | ~$2–5 | Buy after domain; create hello@ with `gddy` |
| Meera's demo domain | Credit, if room | Cart price | One full launch for the recording |
| Meera's own mailbox | Credit, if room | Another Pro Light month | Likely skip; test orders go to app mailbox (say so) |

If money runs out: skip Meera's domain; full launch on a subdomain; show purchase in dry-run. SMTP tip: if login fails use `smtpout.secureserver.net` with the full address as username.

**Claude: $100, API only, for the product.** None of it for Claude Code.
- ~3 small calls per launch (cents).
- Strong model only for Reader; cheap for Namer + Doctor.
- Dev: saved fixtures, not live calls, for UI work.
- Live link: per-visitor limit, max-token cap per call, daily spend cap.
- Check spend in the Claude console daily.

---

## 11. Submission (HackerEarth, by Nov 20)

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Title | LaunchWitness: from description to a proven, live business |
| Description | Demo video link (YouTube, unlisted) first line, then project brief + link to the build replay page |
| Theme | Open Innovation |
| Demo Link | Live app URL on the app domain, with a free sandbox launch judges can try |
| Repository URL | GitHub repo |
| Source Code | Zip of repo, no secrets |
| Additional File | Project brief PDF |

Build process for judges: one combined claude-replay page of all Claude Code sessions, hosted at `https://<APP_DOMAIN>/build`, plus `docs/BUILD_LOG.md`.

---

## 12. Demo video script (3 minutes, screen + voiceover, no face)

| Time | Scene | On screen | Voiceover |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Meera | Instagram: price list highlight, orders in DMs | "Meera has customers. She doesn't have a business online." |

7	Session 9: UPI pay link, order status tracking, trust and safety
8	
9	**Positioning (decided in session 8.5): proof first, generation last.** Pitch: "Airo builds your website. LaunchWitness proves it can take a customer's order, fixes it when it can't, and keeps watching after launch." Every new piece below should feed the proof: the UPI-link and status-page checks are launch checks; seller-facing copy talks about "your shop is ready for customers", not "your website is generated". Infra facts: app domain `launchwitness.com`, mailbox `hello@launchwitness.com` (GoDaddy Professional Email, secureserver.net), VPS arrives Wed Nov 18, demo shop `meerasbakes.launchwitness.com`.

11	Follow the session ritual in CLAUDE.md: read CLAUDE.md and docs/PROGRESS.md, post a plan, and WAIT for my OK.
12	
13	## Goal
14	Sellers need payment and order tracking, and the platform needs basic protection against abuse. No payment gateway (it needs per-seller KYC and can't be one-click). Use what Indian home sellers actually use: UPI, WhatsApp links and a simple status page.
15	
16	## Scope
17	
18	### Orders
19	1. **Order form fields** (on the session-8 template; stay generic, nothing trade-specific):
20	   - Date needed. Enforce `min_notice_days` on the server in India time (Asia/Kolkata): the earliest allowed date is today + notice days; no past dates; at most 60 days ahead.
21	   - Pickup vs delivery, offered only as the profile allows (`pickup_available`, `delivery_available`). Address is required only for delivery.
22	   - Quantity per item (the basket already exists).
23	   - "Message on the item": already shown only when `allow_item_message` is on (a profile field, default off; no presets). Keep it that way.
24	   - Phone (already there; keep the 10-digit check).
25	2. **Order ID:** `LW-` + 8 characters from an unambiguous alphabet (no 0/O/1/I), e.g. `LW-4F2K7Q9M`, from `secrets`, unique, stored next to the internal id. Store orders with a status history (status, time, who changed it).
26	3. **Server-side totals:** price × quantity from the saved menu, plus `delivery_fee_inr` only when delivery is chosen. Never trust client prices (the form already ignores them; keep the test). Extras can't be ordered alone (already enforced).
27	4. **UPI pay:** after submitting, show "Pay ₹X via UPI". On phones, a prefilled link `upi://pay?pa=<VPA>&pn=<name>&am=<amount>&cu=INR&tn=<order ID>`; on laptops, a QR of the same link. Show "Your UPI app should show: <upi_display_name>" when set. Validate the VPA format when the profile is saved (already done). If the seller has no UPI ID, say "The shop will tell you how to pay" instead. No money ever passes through us.
28	5. **Status page** `/o/<order id>` on the seller's own site: Received → Confirmed → Paid → Preparing → Ready / Out for delivery → **Delivered / Picked up**, or Cancelled (from any state before Delivered; if it was Paid, show "The shop will refund you on UPI"). No illegal jumps. No PII beyond the customer's first name and the items. Rate-limited per visitor; unknown IDs get a plain 404.
29	6. **Seller controls** on her existing owner secret link: list orders (newest first, filter by status), change status, "Mark paid" after checking her UPI app. **Test orders from the launch check are marked and hidden from this list by default.**

# Session 9 prompt — UPI pay link, order tracking, trust and safety

Paste this as the first message of session 9.

---

Session 9: UPI pay link, order status tracking, trust and safety

**Positioning (decided in session 8.5): proof first, generation last.** Pitch: "Airo builds your website. LaunchWitness proves it can take a customer's order, fixes it when it can't, and keeps watching after launch." Every new piece below should feed the proof: the UPI-link and status-page checks are launch checks; seller-facing copy talks about "your shop is ready for customers", not "your website is generated". Infra facts: app domain `launchwitness.com`, mailbox `hello@launchwitness.com` (GoDaddy Professional Email, secureserver.net), VPS arrives Wed Nov 18, demo shop `meerasbakes.launchwitness.com`.

Follow the session ritual in CLAUDE.md: read CLAUDE.md and docs/PROGRESS.md, post a plan, and WAIT for my OK.

## Goal
Sellers need payment and order tracking, and the platform needs basic protection against abuse. No payment gateway (it needs per-seller KYC and can't be one-click). Use what Indian home sellers actually use: UPI, WhatsApp links and a simple status page.

## Scope

### Orders
1. **Order form fields** (on the session-8 template; stay generic, nothing trade-specific):
   - Date needed. Enforce `min_notice_days` on the server in India time (Asia/Kolkata): the earliest allowed date is today + notice days; no past dates; at most 60 days ahead.
   - Pickup vs delivery, offered only as the profile allows (`pickup_available`, `delivery_available`). Address is required only for delivery.
   - Quantity per item (the basket already exists).
   - "Message on the item": already shown only when `allow_item_message` is on (a profile field, default off; no presets). Keep it that way.
   - Phone (already there; keep the 10-digit check).
2. **Order ID:** `LW-` + 8 characters from an unambiguous alphabet (no 0/O/1/I), e.g. `LW-4F2K7Q9M`, from `secrets`, unique, stored next to the internal id. Store orders with a status history (status, time, who changed it).
3. **Server-side totals:** price × quantity from the saved menu, plus `delivery_fee_inr` only when delivery is chosen. Never trust client prices (the form already ignores them; keep the test). Extras can't be ordered alone (already enforced).
4. **UPI pay:** after submitting, show "Pay ₹X via UPI". On phones, a prefilled link `upi://pay?pa=<VPA>&pn=<name>&am=<amount>&cu=INR&tn=<order ID>`; on laptops, a QR of the same link. Show "Your UPI app should show: <upi_display_name>" when set. Validate the VPA format when the profile is saved (already done). If the seller has no UPI ID, say "The shop will tell you how to pay" instead. No money ever passes through us.
5. **Status page** `/o/<order id>` on the seller's own site: Received → Confirmed → Paid → Preparing → Ready / Out for delivery → **Delivered / Picked up**, or Cancelled (from any state before Delivered; if it was Paid, show "The shop will refund you on UPI"). No illegal jumps. No PII beyond the customer's first name and the items. Rate-limited per visitor; unknown IDs get a plain 404.
6. **Seller controls** on her existing owner secret link: list orders (newest first, filter by status), change status, "Mark paid" after checking her UPI app. **Test orders from the launch check are marked and hidden from this list by default.**
7. **The seller must not miss an order.** This is the biggest gap. Use only free `wa.me` links:
   - The new-order email goes to the shop mailbox **and** her personal email (`owner_email`). It includes the order ID, the status link and the pay amount.
   - The customer's success screen has **"Send this order to <shop> on WhatsApp"** (a prefilled `wa.me` link to the seller with the order ID, items and total), plus the status link and a "share" link.
   - Each order in the seller's list has **"Tell the customer on WhatsApp"**, with a ready-typed message for the current status and the status link.
8. **New launch checks** (Checker + Doctor playbook):
   - A test order produces a valid UPI link with the right amount and order ID (marked **skipped, not failed**, when the seller has no UPI ID).
   - The status page loads and reflects a status change.
   Each needs a plain-sentence Doctor explanation and an allowed fix, or is marked "cannot auto-fix" with the reason.

### Trust and safety
9. **Email verification before any real launch.** The owner's personal email is confirmed with a one-time link (store only a hash of the token; it expires after 24 h; resend is rate-limited). A real launch (not practice) is refused with a plain message until it's verified. The review screen shows whether it's verified.
10. **Claude policy check (hold, never launch).** One cheap-model call on the saved profile before a real launch: is this shop OK to put live? The reply is `{ok, reason}`, where reason is one plain sentence. If it isn't OK, the business is "held for review" and the launch stops with a plain message. Only the team (admin) can release it; Claude can never launch or release anything. If Claude is unavailable, hold rather than launch. Treat the seller's text as data (prompt-injection test). Use fixtures for OK, hold and injection; no live calls this session.
11. **"Report this shop"** link in every seller site's footer: a short form (reason + optional note, honeypot, per-visitor limit). It's stored, audited and emailed to the team mailbox.
12. **Admin pause switch** (team only, on the report page): a paused shop shows a plain "This shop is paused" page and refuses new orders; existing status pages still open. The owner gets an email. Unpause is admin-only. Everything is audited.

## Rules
- No payment gateway, SMS or WhatsApp Business API. Note "Connect Razorpay (after seller KYC)" as future work in SPEC and the judge Q&A (already added in session 8; keep it accurate).
- Works in fixture mode; no live Claude calls needed this session. The policy-check fixtures are hand-written (`_note`) until captured on the owner's laptop.
- Never print or read .env, never paste keys.
- Template stays generic: nothing specific to one seller or trade; no per-business CSS; no "Verified" label anywhere.

## Done when
- Tests cover: notice-date enforcement (in India time, including around midnight), server-side totals incl. the delivery fee only for delivery, UPI link encoding (spaces, ₹ amounts, special characters in names, `&` and `#`), order ID unguessability (alphabet, length, uniqueness, no sequential IDs on public pages), status transitions (no illegal jumps), the status page leaking no PII (no phone, address or surname), owner-link auth on every seller endpoint, test orders hidden from the seller's list, the personal-email copy of new orders, both WhatsApp hand-off links, the 2 new checks passing, failing and skipping correctly, email verification blocking a real launch, the policy check holding (and never releasing), report → stored + emailed, and pause → no new orders.
- Full suite green (same 2 skipped).
- Screenshots of form → pay → status page → seller order list on mobile and desktop saved to `docs/screenshots/s9/`, using at least 3 of the session-8 gallery sellers (one with no UPI ID).
- Update PROGRESS + BUILD_LOG, save the transcript, rebuild replay, run the secret scan, open the PR and merge once tests pass.

# RUNBOOK — M1: put LaunchWitness live on the GoDaddy VPS

Copy-paste steps, in order. Each step ends with **✔ Check**: don't go on until it passes.
Commands marked `(laptop)` run on your computer, `(vps)` on the server.
Replace `<APP_DOMAIN>` (= `launchwitness.com`) and `<VPS_IP>` everywhere.

Rules that still apply (CLAUDE.md): secrets live **only** in the server's `.env`; purchases are made by you on godaddy.com with the hackathon credit; never paste a password into chat, a commit or a file other than `.env`.

> **About `gddy`:** the exact `gddy` sub-commands below are marked *confirm with `gddy tree`*. They were written without access to your CLI version. Run `gddy tree` (or `gddy <command> --help`) first and adjust. Each step also has a REST API or godaddy.com fallback that does the same thing.

---

## 0. Purchases — done (Nov 15)

Already in the GoDaddy account. **Buy nothing else**: $2.37 credit left (expires Nov 23), no card on file.

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| App domain `launchwitness.com` | Bought, 1 year (renews Nov 2027 at $22.99). `launchwitness.in` was NOT bought. |
| Mailbox `hello@launchwitness.com` | Bought: GoDaddy Professional Email **Pro Light** (secureserver.net backend, not Titan), **1 month**. $5.99/mo monthly; $23.88/yr on a 1-yr term (`EMAIL_PLAN_ESTIMATE_USD=23.88`). **Expires ~Dec 15; auto-renew will lapse** (no card). |
| Mail DNS | Set by GoDaddy: MX `smtp.secureserver.net` / `mailstore1.secureserver.net`, SPF `include:secureserver.net -all`, DKIM ×2, DMARC `p=quarantine`. Leave them alone. |
| Docker VPS | **Free, arrives Wed Nov 18. Do NOT buy one.** |
| Demo seller domain | Not bought. The demo shop is `meerasbakes.launchwitness.com` via the wildcard record (step 6). |

`A @` still points at GoDaddy's parked WebsiteBuilder page. Don't change any DNS until the VPS exists (step 6).

**✔ Check:** `python scripts/list_godaddy_domains.py` lists `launchwitness.com` as ACTIVE (read-only, uses the prod keys in `.env`, never prints them). When the VPS arrives, write down its IP as `<VPS_IP>`.

## 1. SSH key and first connection

```bash
# (laptop) make a key just for this server (press Enter for no passphrase, or set one)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/launchwitness -C "launchwitness-vps"
cat ~/.ssh/launchwitness.pub        # paste this public key into the VPS dashboard (SSH keys)
```

If the dashboard instead gives you a root password, add the key once with:
`ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness.pub root@<VPS_IP>`.

```bash
# (laptop) connect
ssh -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness root@<VPS_IP>
```

Optional but recommended (vps): a non-root user and a firewall.

```bash
adduser --disabled-password [REDACTED] "" lw && usermod -aG sudo lw
mkdir -p /home/lw/.ssh && cp ~/.ssh/authorized_keys /home/lw/.ssh/ && chown -R lw:lw /home/lw/.ssh
echo 'lw ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/lw
ufw allow OpenSSH && ufw allow 80/tcp && ufw allow 443/tcp && ufw allow 443/udp && ufw --force enable
# from now on: ssh -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness lw@<VPS_IP>
```

**✔ Check:** `ssh -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness lw@<VPS_IP> 'whoami && sudo ufw status'` prints `lw` and shows 22/80/443 allowed.

## 2. Install Docker

```bash
# (vps)
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER" && newgrp docker
```

**✔ Check:** `docker run --rm hello-world` prints "Hello from Docker!" and `docker compose version` prints v2.x.

## 3. Clone the repo

```bash
# (vps)
sudo apt-get install -y git
git clone https://github.com/aarushitandon0/LaunchWitness.git ~/LaunchWitness
cd ~/LaunchWitness && git log --oneline -1
```

(Private repo? Create a read-only **deploy key**: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/gh_deploy` on the VPS, add the `.pub` under GitHub → repo → Settings → Deploy keys, then clone with `git@github.com:aarushitandon0/LaunchWitness.git` and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -i ~/.ssh/gh_deploy'`.)

**✔ Check:** `ls ~/LaunchWitness/deploy` shows `Dockerfile docker-compose.yml docker-compose.prod.yml Caddyfile Caddyfile.prod`.

## 4. Point DNS at the VPS (A record + wildcard)

Two A records on `<APP_DOMAIN>`: `@` → `<VPS_IP>` (the app) and `*` → `<VPS_IP>` (free seller addresses like `meera.<APP_DOMAIN>`).

With `gddy` (*confirm with `gddy tree`*; the shape is "add/replace a DNS record"):

```bash
gddy tree | grep -i -A3 dns                         # find the record command
gddy dns records set <APP_DOMAIN> A @ <VPS_IP>     # confirm syntax
gddy dns records set <APP_DOMAIN> A '*' <VPS_IP>   # confirm syntax
```

Same thing with the GoDaddy REST API (production keys from developer.godaddy.com; keep them in your shell only):

```bash
read -rs GD_KEY && read -rs GD_SECRET              # type them, nothing is echoed
for name in @ '*'; do
  curl -sS -X PUT "https://api.godaddy.com/v1/domains/<APP_DOMAIN>/records/A/$name" \
    -H "Authorization: sso-key $GD_KEY:$GD_SECRET" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '[{"data":"<VPS_IP>","ttl":600}]' && echo " set A $name"
done
unset GD_KEY GD_SECRET
```

Fallback: godaddy.com → *Domain* → *DNS* → *Add record* → Type **A**, Name `@`, Value `<VPS_IP>`; again with Name `*`.

**✔ Check (wait up to an hour):**
`dig +short <APP_DOMAIN> @ns01.domaincontrol.com` and `dig +short test123.<APP_DOMAIN> @ns01.domaincontrol.com` both print `<VPS_IP>` (use the NS names your zone shows: `dig +short NS <APP_DOMAIN>`).

## 5. Create `.env` on the server only

```bash
# (vps)
cd ~/LaunchWitness && cp .env.example .env && chmod 600 .env && nano .env
```

Fill in (leave anything not listed at its default):

| Variable | Value | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_DOMAIN` | `<APP_DOMAIN>` | the domain you bought |
| `APP_BASE_URL` | `https://<APP_DOMAIN>` | — |
| `ADMIN_TOKEN` | 32+ random chars | `openssl rand -base64 32` on the VPS (admin is **off** while it's `change-me` or < 16 chars) |
| `SERVER_IP` | `<VPS_IP>` | VPS dashboard |
| `USE_FAKES` | `true` for now | step 10 explains when to set `false` |
| `VISITOR_DESCRIBES_PER_DAY` / `VISITOR_LAUNCHES_PER_DAY` / `VISITOR_CONTACTS_PER_DAY` | `5` / `3` / `5` | defaults; judges' limits |
| `MONITOR_ENABLED` | `true` | (forced on by `docker-compose.prod.yml` anyway) |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | your key, or empty | console.anthropic.com → API keys (only when you decide to go live) |
| `CLAUDE_MODE` | `fixture` (→ `live` later) | keep `fixture` until the key exists and you approve live calls |
| `CLAUDE_MODEL_STRONG` / `CLAUDE_MODEL_CHEAP` | defaults | Reader / Namer + Doctor |
| `CLAUDE_MAX_TOKENS` / `CLAUDE_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` | `1500` / `3` | budget guards |
| `GODADDY_ENV` | `ote` (→ `prod` only when you decide) | — |
| `GODADDY_API_KEY` / `GODADDY_API_SECRET` | production key + secret | developer.godaddy.com → API Keys → *Production* |
| `GODADDY_OTE_API_KEY` / `GODADDY_OTE_API_SECRET` | OTE key + secret | developer.godaddy.com → API Keys → *OTE* |
| `ALLOW_PURCHASE` | `false` | **never change** (you buy on godaddy.com) |
| `MAX_SPEND_USD` | `15` | **never raise casually** |
| `EMAIL_PLAN_ESTIMATE_USD` | real yearly Pro Light price | your GoDaddy cart (step 0) |
| `SMTP_HOST` / `SMTP_PORT` | `smtpout.secureserver.net` / `465` | GoDaddy Professional Email settings (587 STARTTLS is the automatic fallback) |
| `SMTP_USER` | `hello@<APP_DOMAIN>` (full address) | step 8 |
| `SMTP_PASSWORD` | the mailbox password | the one you set in step 8 (or the email GoDaddy sends the account owner) |
| `IMAP_HOST` / `IMAP_PORT` | `imap.secureserver.net` / `993` | GoDaddy Professional Email settings |
| `IMAP_USER` / `IMAP_PASSWORD` | same address and password as SMTP | step 8 |
| `DATABASE_URL` | default | SQLite on the `app-data` volume |
| `CADDYFILE` | `Caddyfile.prod` | (the prod compose file forces it anyway) |

**✔ Check:** `ls -l .env` shows `-rw-------`, and `git status --short` does **not** list `.env`.

## 6. Start the stack with HTTPS (Caddyfile.prod)

```bash
# (vps)
cd ~/LaunchWitness
docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build
docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml ps
```

(Tip: `alias lwc='docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml'` in `~/.bashrc`, then `lwc ps`, `lwc logs -f app`.)

**✔ Check:** `ps` shows `app` and `caddy` as **(healthy)**; from your laptop `curl -sS https://<APP_DOMAIN>/api/health` prints `{"ok":true,"env":"ote"}` without a certificate error; the landing page opens on your phone.
(If Caddy can't get a certificate: `lwc logs caddy | tail -50`; usually DNS from step 4 hasn't spread yet, or port 80/443 is closed.)

## 7. Nightly database backup

```bash
# (vps)
bash scripts/backup_db.sh                      # first backup now
( crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '15 3 * * * cd ~/LaunchWitness && bash scripts/backup_db.sh >> backups/backup.log 2>&1' ) | crontab -
```

**✔ Check:** `ls -l backups/` shows `launchwitness-<time>.db` (mode `-rw-------`). Restore, if ever needed: `bash scripts/backup_db.sh --restore backups/launchwitness-<time>.db`.

## 8. Create the mailbox `hello@<APP_DOMAIN>`

> **Already done (Nov 15):** `hello@launchwitness.com` exists on GoDaddy Professional Email (secureserver.net) and its DNS records are set. Just copy the address + password into the VPS `.env` and restart; the check below uses GoDaddy webmail (email.secureserver.net), not Titan.

gddy email accounts create hello@<APP_DOMAIN>             # confirm syntax; set a strong password when asked

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
