7	---
8	
9	## 1. Pitch
10	
11	**One line for judges:** "Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy and proves everything works before your first customer arrives."
12	
13	LaunchWitness takes a small seller from a few lines of description to a live business on her own domain: website, business email, and an order form that reaches her inbox. Then it checks every part for real, fixes or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps checking lightly afterwards.
14	
15	**What makes it different.** Most AI builders stop at "your site is ready." LaunchWitness shows the proof: a real test order arriving in her inbox, every check green, and a report with the time each one passed. The safety rules (approve before spending, preview before changing, undo on failure) are what let an AI be trusted to spend money and change settings for a non-technical owner.
16	
17	**Why it fits GoDaddy.** Small businesses buying a domain, a website and an email is GoDaddy's core business. LaunchWitness uses GoDaddy's Domains, DNS and Email as the engine, not decoration. GoDaddy's own AI tools already help people get online; LaunchWitness adds the missing piece: proof that it all works, before customers find out it doesn't.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. Problem and the story
22	
23	Small sellers either never get their own online presence, or they get one that is quietly broken.
24	
25	1. **They don't start, because setup is technical.** A GoDaddy survey found 63% of India's small businesses had no website; of those planning one, only 15% owned a domain, and 30% wanted someone to build and manage it for them (DNA India). The survey is several years old: present it as background, not today's figure.
26	2. **When they do start, it's often half-working.** A March 2026 analysis put DMARC adoption at 44.9% for small businesses vs 75.3% for large enterprises (Cross-Sector DNS & Email Security). A scan of 200 small and mid-size business domains found 36% missing SPF and over two-thirds with no DMARC record (DEV). Result: order emails land in spam, and the owner never knows — she just thinks business is slow.
27	3. **AI could do the setup, but isn't trusted to.** Buying a domain and changing settings means spending money and risking email. An owner who can't read a DNS record can't check an agent's work.
28	
29	Open question: find one current (2025–26) India-specific figure on small businesses without websites before the deck.
30	
31	**Demo persona: Meera.** Meera sells custom cakes from home and takes orders over Instagram DMs. No website, no business email, never touched DNS. She types two lines and pastes her price list. A few minutes later she has meerabakes.in with her real menu and prices, hello@meerabakes.in, and an order form that lands in that inbox. Before she shares the link with a single customer, LaunchWitness places a test order, watches it arrive, and shows her: **"Your business is ready for customers."**

35	## 3. How it works (user flow)
36	
37	Seven steps from description to proof; Meera does four of them, and only one costs money.
38	
39	1. **Describe.** A few lines + price list (typed, pasted or photo). No WhatsApp/Instagram API.
40	   - Claude (one call) returns the business profile (name, products, prices, hours, area, tone) **plus** the site copy (tagline, about, item descriptions) **plus** how customers order: selling point, days of notice, pickup / delivery and delivery charge, whether customers may add a message for an item, the name the seller's UPI app shows, and her food licence (FSSAI) number if given. Plain code then tidies the reply (delivery is never a menu item; extras such as toppers are marked as extras; ordering rules leave the hours line).
41	   - **Scope guard (v1 = sellers who take orders).** If the business needs bookings rather than orders (salon, tuition, clinic, classes), the Reader says so in one plain sentence and no shop is built.
42	2. **Review.** She sees the profile as a form and fixes anything wrong. No AI.
43	3. **Pick a name.** Claude (one small call) suggests ~10 domain names; code checks real availability + price; shows the best 3.
44	4. **Preview and approve.** Code fills the ONE fixed template, the same for every seller (no per-business code or CSS; category colours come from a fixed palette by position): header with short badges taken only from her data, menu with prices and an Add button per item (a basket that also works without JavaScript; long menus get two columns and a search box), extras listed apart, about, hours, pickup/delivery, "Order on WhatsApp" link (`wa.me`), UPI QR with "Your UPI app should show: <name>", optional FSSAI number in the footer, privacy page. No "Verified" label anywhere. One approval card lists the domain, total cost and every setting to be made. **Nothing is bought or changed until she taps Approve.**
45	5. **Launch.** Code only: back up DNS, buy the domain (or use a free sandbox subdomain), point it at the server, set up email, put the site live with HTTPS. Each step streams on screen.
46	6. **Launch check.** Code checks the site opens, HTTPS is valid, email settings are correct, then places a real test order through her form. If anything fails, the Doctor explains it in one sentence, applies a safe fix or undoes the change, and re-checks until green.
47	7. **Report and watch.** Report headed **"Your business is ready for customers"**: every check, result, time passed. After launch, the same checks re-run lightly on a timer and alert her if something breaks.
48	
49	**Two launch modes, same code:**
50	- **Sandbox launch** at `<slug>.<APP_DOMAIN>`: free, real DNS writes on the app's own domain, real checks. Used for development, rehearsals and judges trying it.
51	- **Full launch** on a purchased domain: run once, for the recorded demo.

100	## 6. Launch checks and repair
101	
102	Repair happens during launch, because that's where setups actually go wrong: settings not spread yet, a certificate failing first time, a mailbox not ready, an email setting missing, a step failing halfway.
103	
104	| Check | How | If it fails |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| Domain points to the site | DNS lookup against GoDaddy's authoritative nameservers (not a cached resolver) | Re-point, wait, re-check |
107	| Site opens over HTTPS | Fetch, validate certificate | Retry certificate, re-check |
108	| Email settings correct | Look up MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Re-add the missing record from the plan |
109	| Test order arrives | Submit the real form; email carries a "Yes, I got it" link | Check mailbox readiness + MX, retry |
110	| Launch finished cleanly | Step log shows every step done | Resume the failed step, or undo DNS from backup |
111	
112	**Repair rules:** max 3 attempts per check, then stop and explain in plain words. Repair never spends money. Every attempt goes to the audit log.
113	
114	**Confirming the test order:** for real sellers the app can't read their inbox (GoDaddy emails mailbox passwords to the account owner only), so the seller taps "Yes, I got it". For the demo mailbox, the checker can also read the inbox over IMAP (password in env).
115	
116	**Demo failure:** during launch one check fails on purpose (e.g. DMARC missing → orders would land in spam). The Doctor explains, re-adds, re-checks to green. The fault is staged — say so if asked.

121	
122	Light monitoring is core; full only if time permits. It re-runs launch checks on a timer (GoDaddy's API has no webhooks).
123	
124	**Light (build now)**
125	
126	| How often | What |
127	|---|---|
128	| Every 15 minutes | Site opens, HTTPS valid |
129	| Daily | DNS + email settings still match launch; days left on certificate and domain |
130	
131	- On failure: re-check once a minute later (rule out blips), then Doctor explains + safe playbook fix.
132	- Anything needing money or her action (renewal, payment): alert only, at 30 / 7 / 1 days before expiry.
133	- Alerts go to her **personal email**, not the business inbox.
134	- "Run checks now" button = same checks on demand (this is how the demo shows it).
135	
136	**Full (if time permits):** daily real test order; change detection ("Was this you? Tap to restore") instead of silent undo; incident history on the report.

142	## 8. Architecture and GoDaddy usage

144	One GoDaddy Docker VPS (4 vCPU / 8 GB, provided at $0) runs everything; GoDaddy and Claude are called as APIs.

148	- **React (Vite):** seller-facing app, built and served as static files.
149	- **SQLite:** profiles, plans, DNS backups, check results, audit log.
150	- **Outside:** Claude API; GoDaddy Domains/DNS/Email (OTE sandbox in dev, `GODADDY_ENV=ote|prod`); SMTP through the app's one mailbox.

"""List the domains in your GoDaddy account (read-only, production API).

One GET to https://api.godaddy.com/v1/domains with
`Authorization: sso-key <GODADDY_API_KEY>:<GODADDY_API_SECRET>`.
It never buys, changes or deletes anything, and never prints the key or secret.

Keys come from the environment, or from the repo's `.env` (git-ignored) if not set there.

Usage (from the repo root):
    python scripts/list_godaddy_domains.py           # table
    python scripts/list_godaddy_domains.py --json    # raw JSON
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

URL = "https://api.godaddy.com/v1/domains?limit=100"
ENV_FILE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".env"
KEYS = ("GODADDY_API_KEY", "GODADDY_API_SECRET")


def read_env_file(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Minimal .env reader: KEY=value, ignores comments and blank lines, strips quotes and inline comments."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    if not path.exists():
        return out
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        value = value.strip()
        if value[:1] in ("'", '"') and value[-1:] == value[:1] and len(value) >= 2:
            value = value[1:-1]
        else:
            value = value.split(" #", 1)[0].strip()
        out[key.strip()] = value
    return out


def credentials() -> tuple[str, str]:
    file_env = read_env_file(ENV_FILE)
    values = [os.environ.get(k) or file_env.get(k, "") for k in KEYS]
    missing = [k for k, v in zip(KEYS, values) if not v]
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"Missing {', '.join(missing)} (set them in .env or the environment). Nothing was sent.")
    return values[0], values[1]


def main() -> int:
    raw = "--json" in sys.argv[1:]
    key, secret = credentials()
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, method="GET", headers={
        "Authorization": f"sso-key {key}:{secret}",
        "Accept": "application/json",
    })
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
            domains = json.load(r)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        # The body is GoDaddy's error JSON (code + message); it never contains our key.
        body = e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]
        print(f"GoDaddy answered HTTP {e.code}: {body}", file=sys.stderr)
        if e.code in (401, 403):
            print("Check that these are PRODUCTION keys (not OTE) and that the account may use the API.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
        print(f"Could not reach api.godaddy.com: {e.reason}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if raw:
        print(json.dumps(domains, indent=2))
        return 0
    if not domains:
        print("No domains in this account.")

Please try again.") name = " ".join(form.get("customer_name", "").split())[:80] phone = form.get("customer_phone", "").strip() note = form.get("note", "").strip()[:1000] if profile.allow_item_message: message = " ".join(form.get("item_message", "").split())[:200] if message: note = f"Message on the item: {message}" + (f"\n{note}" if note else "") if not name: raise OrderInvalid("Please add your name so we know who the order is for.") if not re.fullmatch(r"\+?[\d\s-]{10,20}", phone) or len(re.sub(r"\D", "", phone)) < 10: raise OrderInvalid("Please add a phone number we can call or WhatsApp (at least 10 digits).") items = [] for i, product in enumerate(profile.products): raw = form.get(f"qty_{i}", "0").strip() or "0" if not raw.isdigit() or int(raw) > MAX_QTY: raise OrderInvalid(f"Please enter a quantity between 0 and {MAX_QTY}.") if int(raw) > 0: items.append({"name": product.name, "qty": int(raw), "price_inr": product.price_inr, "addon": product.addon}) if not items and not note: raise OrderInvalid("Please choose at least one item, or tell us what you'd like in the note.") if items and all(it["addon"] for it in items): raise OrderInvalid("Extras go with another item. Please choose an item too.") for it in items: del it["addon"] total = sum(it["qty"] * it["price_inr"] for it in items) return {"customer_name": name, "customer_phone": phone, "note": note, "items": items, "total_inr": total} def order_email(business: Business, profile: Profile, order: Order, items: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, str]: from app.sites.render import format_inr test = "[TEST] " if order.is_test else "" subject = f"{test}New order for {profile.name} from {order.customer_name} (#{order.id})" lines = [f"New order #{order.id} for {profile.name}", "", f"Customer: {order.customer_name}", f"Phone: {order.customer_phone}", ""] lines += [f"- {it['qty']} x {it['name']} @ {format_inr(it['price_inr'])} = {format_inr(it['qty'] * it['price_inr'])}" for it in items] or ["(no items chosen; see note)"] lines += ["", f"Estimated total: {format_inr(order.total_inr)}"] if order.note: lines += ["", "Note from customer:", order.note] lines += ["", f"Placed: {order.created_at:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC", "Sent by LaunchWitness"] return subject, "\n".join(lines) def place_order(session: Session, mailer: Mailer, *, business: Business, profile: Profile, data: dict, mail_to: str, is_test: bool = False) -> Order: order = Order(business_id=business.id, customer_name=data["customer_name"], customer_phone=data["customer_phone"], items_json=json.dumps(data["items"], ensure_ascii=False), total_inr=data["total_inr"], note=data["note"], is_test=is_test) session.add(order) session.commit() session.refresh(order) audit.record(session, actor="checker" if is_test else "customer", action="order_placed", target=f"order:{order.id}", result="ok", business_id=business.id, detail=f"{len(data['items'])} item(s), total {data['total_inr']}") subject, body = order_email(business, profile, order, data["items"]) try: order.email_message_id = mailer.send(to=mail_to, subject=subject, body=body) order.email_status = "sent" result, detail = "ok", f"to app mailbox, {order.email_message_id}" except Exception as e: # keep the order even if the mail server is down order.email_status = "failed" result, detail = "failed", type(e).__name__ session.add(order) session.commit() session.refresh(order) audit.record(session, actor="system", action="order_email", target=f"order:{order.id}", result=result, business_id=business.id, detail=detail) return order """Seller site pages, chosen by the Host header (see app.sites.hosts).""" from typing import Annotated from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse from sqlmodel import Session from app.agents.reader import Profile from app.config import Settings, get_settings from app.db import get_session from app.mail.smtp import Mailer, get_mailer from app.models import Business from app.sites.hosts import business_for_host, normalize_host, subdomain_label from app.sites.orders import OrderInvalid, parse_order_form, place_order from app.sites.render import render_site router = APIRouter(tags=["seller-site"]) NOT_SET_UP = """ Site not found

This site isn't set up yet

Please check the address. If this is your shop, finish setting it up in LaunchWitness.

""" def seller_for_request(request: Request, settings: Settings, session: Session) -> tuple[Business, Profile] | None: """(business, profile) when the Host is a seller site; None when it's the app itself. Raises 404 for an unknown

"""All outside services the launch engine uses, bundled so they can be swapped.

USE_FAKES=true (default): one shared in-memory "fake world" per process
(GoDaddy zones, availability, mailbox, authoritative DNS answering from the
fake zones, HTTP probe). Nothing real changes. USE_FAKES=false: real clients;
the parts not built yet raise NotImplementedError (see PROGRESS.md).
"""

import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from functools import lru_cache

from app.checks.dns_resolver import DnsResolver, ZoneBackedResolver
from app.checks.http_probe import FakeHttpProbe, HttpProbe, RealHttpProbe
from app.config import Settings, get_settings
from app.godaddy.availability import AvailabilityChecker, FakeAvailabilityChecker, GoDaddyAvailabilityChecker
from app.godaddy.client import FakeGoDaddyClient, GoDaddy, GoDaddyClient
from app.godaddy.email import FakeMailboxProvider, MailboxProvider, TitanMailboxProvider
from app.mail.imap import FakeInboxReader, ImapInboxReader, InboxReader
from app.mail.smtp import FakeMailer, Mailer, SmtpMailer


class DeliveringFakeMailer(FakeMailer):
    """Practice mode: 'sent' mail lands in the fake inbox, like a working mailbox would."""

    def __init__(self, inbox: FakeInboxReader, sender: str):
        super().__init__()
        self.inbox, self.sender, self.drop = inbox, sender, False

    def send(self, *, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> str:
        message_id = super().send(to=to, subject=subject, body=body)
        if not self.drop:
            self.inbox.deliver(sender=self.sender, to=to, subject=subject, body=body)
        return message_id


@dataclass
class Integrations:
    godaddy: GoDaddy
    availability: AvailabilityChecker
    mailbox: MailboxProvider
    dns: DnsResolver  # must ask GoDaddy's AUTHORITATIVE nameservers, not a cache
    http: HttpProbe
    mailer: Mailer  # used by the launch check's test order
    inbox: InboxReader  # demo mailbox, to prove the test order arrived
    sleep: Callable[[float], None] = field(default=time.sleep)
    fake: bool = False


def fake_integrations(settings: Settings, sleep: Callable[[float], None] | None = None) -> Integrations:
    gd = FakeGoDaddyClient(owned={settings.app_domain})
    inbox = FakeInboxReader()
    return Integrations(
        godaddy=gd,
        availability=FakeAvailabilityChecker(),
        mailbox=FakeMailboxProvider(existing={settings.smtp_user}),
        dns=ZoneBackedResolver(gd),
        http=FakeHttpProbe(settings),
        mailer=DeliveringFakeMailer(inbox, settings.smtp_user),
        inbox=inbox,
        sleep=sleep or (lambda _s: None),
        fake=True,
    )


def real_integrations(settings: Settings) -> Integrations:
    from app.checks.dns_resolver import RealDnsResolver

    return Integrations(
        godaddy=GoDaddyClient(settings),
        availability=GoDaddyAvailabilityChecker(),
        mailbox=TitanMailboxProvider(),
        # TODO(real): pass GoDaddy's authoritative nameserver IPs (ns*.domaincontrol.com) for the zone.
        dns=RealDnsResolver(),
        http=RealHttpProbe(),
        mailer=SmtpMailer(settings),
        inbox=ImapInboxReader(settings),
    )


@lru_cache
def _shared_fakes() -> Integrations:
    return fake_integrations(get_settings())


def get_integrations() -> Integrations:
    """FastAPI dependency: the server's own integrations (real when USE_FAKES=false). Tests override this."""
    settings = get_settings()
    return _shared_fakes() if settings.use_fakes else real_integrations(settings)


def get_practice_integrations() -> Integrations:
    """FastAPI dependency: the shared fake world, used for practice businesses. Tests override this."""
    return _shared_fakes()


def for_business(business, server: Integrations, practice: Integrations) -> Integrations:
    """Practice businesses NEVER get real integrations, whatever the server mode."""
    return practice if business.practice or server.fake else server
"""Read the demo inbox (IMAP over SSL) to prove a test order arrived."""

import email
import imaplib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from email.header import decode_header, make_header
from typing import Protocol

from app.config import Settings


@dataclass
class InboxMessage:
    sender: str
    to: str
    subject: str
    body: str


class InboxReader(Protocol):
    def find(self, *, subject_contains: str) -> list[InboxMessage]: ...


class ImapInboxReader:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings):
        self.host = settings.imap_host
        self.port = settings.imap_port
        self.user = settings.imap_user
        self._password = settings.imap_password

    def find(self, *, subject_contains: str) -> list[InboxMessage]:
        out: list[InboxMessage] = []
        with imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(self.host, self.port, timeout=30) as conn:
            conn.login(self.user, self._password.get_secret_value())
            conn.select("INBOX", readonly=True)
            _, data = conn.search(None, "SUBJECT", f'"{subject_contains}"')
            for num in data[0].split():
                _, parts = conn.fetch(num, "(RFC822)")
                msg = email.message_from_bytes(parts[0][1])
                body_part = msg.get_body(preferencelist=("plain",)) if hasattr(msg, "get_body") else None
                payload = body_part.get_payload(decode=True) if body_part else msg.get_payload(decode=True)
                out.append(
                    InboxMessage(
                        sender=str(msg.get("From", "")),
                        to=str(msg.get("To", "")),
                        subject=str(make_header(decode_header(msg.get("Subject", "")))),
                        body=(payload or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
                    )
                )
        return out


class FakeInboxReader:
    """Holds messages in memory; `deliver()` simulates mail arriving."""

    def __init__(self, messages: list[InboxMessage] | None = None):
        self.messages = list(messages or [])

    def deliver(self, *, sender: str, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
        self.messages.append(InboxMessage(sender=sender, to=to, subject=subject, body=body))

    def find(self, *, subject_contains: str) -> list[InboxMessage]:
        return [m for m in self.messages if subject_contains in m.subject]
"""Business mailbox (Titan via GoDaddy), behind one interface.

Step rules (SPEC §9): create or adopt, poll until ready, retry on failure, never undo.
The real provider is a stub to fill in (see PROGRESS.md: Real integration TODO).
"""

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

# Titan mail records. TODO(real): confirm exact values for GoDaddy-sold Titan.
TITAN_MX = [(10, "mx1.titan.email"), (20, "mx2.titan.email")]
TITAN_SPF = "v=spf1 include:spf.titan.email ~all"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Mailbox:
    address: str
    status: str  # "pending" | "ready"


class MailboxProvider(Protocol):
    def find(self, address: str) -> Mailbox | None: ...
    def create(self, address: str) -> Mailbox: ...
    def status(self, address: str) -> str: ...
    def dkim(self, domain: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """(record name, TXT value), available once the mailbox domain is set up."""
        ...


class FakeMailboxProvider:
    def __init__(self, ready_after_polls: int = 1, fail_creates: int = 0, existing: set[str] | None = None):
        self.ready_after_polls = ready_after_polls
        self.fail_creates = fail_creates
        self.boxes: dict[str, int] = {a: 10**6 for a in (existing or ())}  # address -> polls seen
        self.calls: list[tuple] = []

    def find(self, address: str) -> Mailbox | None:
        self.calls.append(("find", address))
        return Mailbox(address, self.status(address)) if address in self.boxes else None

    def create(self, address: str) -> Mailbox:
        self.calls.append(("create", address))
        if self.fail_creates > 0:
            self.fail_creates -= 1
            raise RuntimeError("fake mailbox service busy")
        self.boxes.setdefault(address, 0)
        return Mailbox(address, "pending")

    def status(self, address: str) -> str:
        if address not in self.boxes:
            return "missing"
        self.boxes[address] += 1
        return "ready" if self.boxes[address] > self.ready_after_polls else "pending"

    def dkim(self, domain: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        return "titan1._domainkey", f"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=FAKE{hashlib.sha256(domain.encode()).hexdigest()[:24]}"


class TitanMailboxProvider:
    """TODO(real): GoDaddy Email/Titan API or `gddy` CLI: find, create, poll status, read DKIM."""

    def find(self, address: str) -> Mailbox | None:
        raise NotImplementedError("Real mailbox provider not implemented yet")

    def create(self, address: str) -> Mailbox:
        raise NotImplementedError("Real mailbox provider not implemented yet")

    def status(self, address: str) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError("Real mailbox provider not implemented yet")

    def dkim(self, domain: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        raise NotImplementedError("Real mailbox provider not implemented yet")
"""SQLite tables. Fields are minimal for M0 and will grow per milestone."""

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel


def utcnow() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


class Business(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    name: str
    owner_email: str = ""
    description: str = ""
    price_list_text: str = ""
    profile_json: str = "{}"  # Reader output (M2)
    # e.g. "meerascakes.in". Unique among real businesses / among practice ones (checked in code),
    # so a practice launch can never hold a real seller's domain.
    domain: str | None = Field(default=None, index=True)
    subdomain: str | None = Field(default=None, unique=True, index=True)  # label under APP_DOMAIN
    status: str = "draft"  # draft | planned | launching | live | failed
    # Practice businesses always run against the fake world (never real GoDaddy/DNS/email).
    # Only businesses created with the admin token on a real server are not practice.
    practice: bool = True
    owner_key_hash: str = ""  # sha256 of the secret owner link token (the token itself is never stored)
    visitor: str = ""  # hashed client IP that created it (daily limit)
    demo_fault: str = ""  # admin demo switch, consumed by the next check run: "" | "dmarc" | "mx"
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)


class Plan(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int = Field(foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    mode: str = "sandbox"  # sandbox | full
    zone: str = ""  # the DNS zone this launch writes to (APP_DOMAIN or the seller's domain)
    site_host: str = ""  # e.g. meera.<APP_DOMAIN> or meerascakes.in
    mailbox: str = ""  # address orders are emailed to
    steps_json: str = "[]"  # [{id, kind, title, detail, status, message, started_at, finished_at}]
    dns_json: str = "[]"  # [{zone, type, name, before: [...], after: [...], say, deferred}]
    total_cost_usd: float = 0.0
    status: str = "draft"  # draft | approved | running | done | failed | blocked
    visitor: str = ""  # hashed client IP that approved it (daily launch limit)
    approved_at: datetime | None = None
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)


class Approval(SQLModel, table=True):
    """The owner's explicit OK for one money-spending action."""

    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int = Field(foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    plan_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="plan.id")
    action: str  # e.g. "buy_domain", "buy_mailbox"
    target: str  # e.g. the domain name
    amount_usd: float  # the exact cost the owner saw and approved
    approved_by: str
    used_at: datetime | None = None
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)


class DnsBackup(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int = Field(foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    plan_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="plan.id", index=True)
    domain: str
    records_json: str
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)


class CheckRun(SQLModel, table=True):
    """One round of checks: after a launch, on "Run checks now", or by the monitor."""

    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int = Field(foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    plan_id: int = Field(foreign_key="plan.id", index=True)
    trigger: str  # launch | manual | monitor_quick | monitor_daily | monitor_recheck
    status: str = "running"  # running | done
    passed: bool | None = None
    repairs_json: str = "[]"  # Doctor attempts: [{check, fixed, attempts: [{explanation, fix_id, applied, message, passed}]}]
    info_json: str = "{}"  # e.g. {"cert_days_left": 80, "domain_days_left": 300}
    started_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)
    finished_at: datetime | None = None


class CheckResult(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int = Field(foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    plan_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="plan.id", index=True)
    run_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="checkrun.id", index=True)
    attempt: int = 0  # 0 = first check, 1..3 = re-check after a repair
    check: str  # e.g. "https", "dns_a", "mx", "test_order"
    passed: bool
    detail: str = ""
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)


class AuditEvent(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    actor: str  # "owner", "system", "executor", "doctor", ...
    action: str
    target: str = ""
    result: str  # "ok" | "blocked" | "failed" | ...
    detail: str = ""
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)


class Alert(SQLModel, table=True):

- sandbox: free site at <subdomain>.<APP_DOMAIN>; one A record on the app's own zone;

class PlanError(ValueError):

def step(sid: str, kind: str, title: str, detail: str) -> dict:
    return {"id": sid, "kind": kind, "title": title, "detail": detail, "status": "pending", "message": "",
            "started_at": None, "finished_at": None}


def _texts(records: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for r in records:
        if r["type"] == "MX":
            out.append(f"{r.get('priority', 10)} {r['data']}")
        else:
            out.append(r["data"])
    return out


def change(zone: str, rtype: str, name: str, before_zone: list[dict], after: list[dict], say: str,
           deferred: bool = False) -> dict:
    before = [r for r in before_zone if r["type"] == rtype and r["name"] == name]
    after = [{"type": rtype, "name": name, "ttl": TTL, **r} for r in after]
    return {"zone": zone, "type": rtype, "name": name, "before": before, "after": after, "say": say,
            "deferred": deferred, "before_text": _texts(before), "after_text": _texts(after)}


def fqdn(zone: str, name: str) -> str:
    return zone if name == "@" else f"{name}.{zone}"


def active_plan(session: Session, business_id: int) -> Plan | None:
    return session.exec(
        select(Plan).where(Plan.business_id == business_id, Plan.status.in_(("approved", "running")))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    ).first()


def build_plan(session: Session, settings: Settings, integ: Integrations, business: Business, *, mode: str,
               domain: str | None = None) -> Plan:
    if active_plan(session, business.id) is not None:
        raise PlanError("A launch is already running for this business. Please wait for it to finish.")
    if not settings.server_ip:
        raise PlanError("The server address isn't configured yet (SERVER_IP).")
    if mode == "sandbox":
        plan = _sandbox(session, settings, integ, business)
    elif mode == "full":
        plan = _full(session, settings, integ, business, (domain or "").strip().lower())
    else:
        raise PlanError("Unknown launch type.")
    session.add(plan)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(plan)
    audit.record(session, actor="planner", action="plan_created", target=plan.site_host, result="ok",
                 business_id=business.id, detail=f"plan #{plan.id} {plan.mode}, ${plan.total_cost_usd:.2f}")
    return plan


def _sandbox(session: Session, settings: Settings, integ: Integrations, business: Business) -> Plan:
    if not business.subdomain:
        raise PlanError("Please choose your website address first.")
    zone, sub = settings.app_domain, business.subdomain
    host = fqdn(zone, sub)
    current = integ.godaddy.get_records(zone)
    changes = [change(zone, "A", sub, current, [{"data": settings.server_ip}],
                      f"Point {host} to your website")]
    steps = [
        step("backup", "backup_dns", "Save a copy of the current settings",
             f"Read every DNS record on {zone} and store it as JSON so any change can be undone."),
        step("point", "point_site", f"Point {host} to your website",

def start_monitor(settings: Settings):

    settings = get_settings()

               run_lifespan: bool = True) -> FastAPI:

    def frontend(

        request: Request,
        settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)],
        session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)],
    ):
        if path.startswith(("api/", "internal/")):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404)
        page = seller_routes.seller_page(path, request, settings, session)
        if page is not None:
            return page
        if path.rstrip("/") == "build":
            if replay_page.is_file():
                return FileResponse(replay_page, media_type="text/html")
            return HTMLResponse(BUILD_COMING_SOON)
        index = frontend_dist / "index.html"
        if not index.is_file():
            return PlainTextResponse("Frontend not built. Run: cd frontend && npm run build")
        return FileResponse(index)

    return app

"""Read the demo inbox (IMAP over SSL) to prove a test order arrived."""

import email
import imaplib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from email.header import decode_header, make_header
from typing import Protocol

from app.config import Settings


@dataclass
class InboxMessage:
    sender: str
    to: str
    subject: str
    body: str


class InboxReader(Protocol):
    def find(self, *, subject_contains: str) -> list[InboxMessage]: ...


class ImapInboxReader:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings):
        self.host = settings.imap_host
        self.port = settings.imap_port
        self.user = settings.imap_user
        self._password = settings.imap_password

    def find(self, *, subject_contains: str) -> list[InboxMessage]:
        out: list[InboxMessage] = []
        with imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(self.host, self.port, timeout=30) as conn:
            conn.login(self.user, self._password.get_secret_value())
            conn.select("INBOX", readonly=True)
            _, data = conn.search(None, "SUBJECT", f'"{subject_contains}"')
            for num in data[0].split():
                _, parts = conn.fetch(num, "(RFC822)")
                msg = email.message_from_bytes(parts[0][1])
                body_part = msg.get_body(preferencelist=("plain",)) if hasattr(msg, "get_body") else None
                payload = body_part.get_payload(decode=True) if body_part else msg.get_payload(decode=True)
                out.append(
                    InboxMessage(
                        sender=str(msg.get("From", "")),
                        to=str(msg.get("To", "")),
                        subject=str(make_header(decode_header(msg.get("Subject", "")))),
                        body=(payload or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
                    )
                )
        return out


class FakeInboxReader:
    """Holds messages in memory; `deliver()` simulates mail arriving."""

    def __init__(self, messages: list[InboxMessage] | None = None):
        self.messages = list(messages or [])

    def deliver(self, *, sender: str, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
        self.messages.append(InboxMessage(sender=sender, to=to, subject=subject, body=body))

    def find(self, *, subject_contains: str) -> list[InboxMessage]:
        return [m for m in self.messages if subject_contains in m.subject]

class FakeMailboxProvider:

        self.ready_after_polls = ready_after_polls
        self.fail_creates = fail_creates
        self.boxes: dict[str, int] = {a: 10**6 for a in (existing or ())}  # address -> polls seen
        self.calls: list[tuple] = []

    def find(self, address: str) -> Mailbox | None:
        self.calls.append(("find", address))
        return Mailbox(address, self.status(address)) if address in self.boxes else None

    def create(self, address: str) -> Mailbox:
        self.calls.append(("create", address))
        if self.fail_creates > 0:
            self.fail_creates -= 1
            raise RuntimeError("fake mailbox service busy")

        return Mailbox(address, "pending")

"""Planner (code only): every step, DNS setting and cost of a launch, before anything happens.

Two modes, same engine:
- sandbox: free site at <subdomain>.<APP_DOMAIN>; one A record on the app's own zone;
  orders go to the app mailbox.
- full: the seller's own domain (bought by the owner, or by the guarded purchase step);
  A record, mailbox, and email records (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC) on that domain.

The plan's `dns_json` is the before/after diff shown on the approval card.
"""

import json
from datetime import datetime

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit
from app.config import Settings
from app.godaddy.email import TITAN_MX, TITAN_SPF
from app.integrations import Integrations
from app.models import Business, Plan
from app.agents.namer import DOMAIN

DKIM_PENDING = "(filled in after your mailbox is created)"
DMARC = "v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; adkim=r; aspf=r"
TTL = 600


class PlanError(ValueError):
    """Message is shown to the seller as-is."""


def step(sid: str, kind: str, title: str, detail: str) -> dict:
    return {"id": sid, "kind": kind, "title": title, "detail": detail, "status": "pending", "message": "",
            "started_at": None, "finished_at": None}


def _texts(records: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for r in records:
        if r["type"] == "MX":
            out.append(f"{r.get('priority', 10)} {r['data']}")
        else:
            out.append(r["data"])
    return out


def change(zone: str, rtype: str, name: str, before_zone: list[dict], after: list[dict], say: str,
           deferred: bool = False) -> dict:
    before = [r for r in before_zone if r["type"] == rtype and r["name"] == name]
    after = [{"type": rtype, "name": name, "ttl": TTL, **r} for r in after]
    return {"zone": zone, "type": rtype, "name": name, "before": before, "after": after, "say": say,
            "deferred": deferred, "before_text": _texts(before), "after_text": _texts(after)}


def fqdn(zone: str, name: str) -> str:
    return zone if name == "@" else f"{name}.{zone}"


def active_plan(session: Session, business_id: int) -> Plan | None:
    return session.exec(
        select(Plan).where(Plan.business_id == business_id, Plan.status.in_(("approved", "running")))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    ).first()


def build_plan(session: Session, settings: Settings, integ: Integrations, business: Business, *, mode: str,
               domain: str | None = None) -> Plan:
    if active_plan(session, business.id) is not None:
        raise PlanError("A launch is already running for this business. Please wait for it to finish.")
    if not settings.server_ip:
        raise PlanError("The server address isn't configured yet (SERVER_IP).")
    if mode == "sandbox":
        plan = _sandbox(session, settings, integ, business)
    elif mode == "full":
        plan = _full(session, settings, integ, business, (domain or "").strip().lower())
    else:
        raise PlanError("Unknown launch type.")
    session.add(plan)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(plan)
    audit.record(session, actor="planner", action="plan_created", target=plan.site_host, result="ok",
                 business_id=business.id, detail=f"plan #{plan.id} {plan.mode}, ${plan.total_cost_usd:.2f}")
    return plan


def _sandbox(session: Session, settings: Settings, integ: Integrations, business: Business) -> Plan:
    if not business.subdomain:
        raise PlanError("Please choose your website address first.")
    zone, sub = settings.app_domain, business.subdomain
    host = fqdn(zone, sub)
    current = integ.godaddy.get_records(zone)
    changes = [change(zone, "A", sub, current, [{"data": settings.server_ip}],
                      f"Point {host} to your website")]
    steps = [
        step("backup", "backup_dns", "Save a copy of the current settings",
             f"Read every DNS record on {zone} and store it as JSON so any change can be undone."),
        step("point", "point_site", f"Point {host} to your website",
             f"Set A {sub}.{zone} → {settings.server_ip} (TTL {TTL})."),
        step("mailbox", "use_app_mailbox", "Send your orders to the LaunchWitness inbox",
             f"Practice launch: order emails go to {settings.smtp_user}."),
        step("wait", "wait_dns", "Wait until the internet sees the change",
             f"Ask GoDaddy's nameservers for {host} until it answers {settings.server_ip}."),
        step("live", "go_live", "Turn your website on",
             f"Mark the business live; HTTPS is issued on first visit (Caddy on-demand TLS, ask = {host})."),
    ]
    return Plan(business_id=business.id, mode="sandbox", zone=zone, site_host=host, mailbox=settings.smtp_user,
                steps_json=json.dumps(steps), dns_json=json.dumps(changes), total_cost_usd=0.0)


def _full(session: Session, settings: Settings, integ: Integrations, business: Business, domain: str) -> Plan:
    if not DOMAIN.match(domain):
        raise PlanError("That doesn't look like a website name we can use (for example: meerascakes.in).")
    if domain == settings.app_domain or domain.endswith("." + settings.app_domain):
        raise PlanError("That name belongs to LaunchWitness. Please pick your own.")
    other = session.exec(select(Business).where(Business.domain == domain, Business.id != business.id,
                                                Business.practice == business.practice)).first()
    if other is not None:
        raise PlanError("That name is already used by another business here.")

    owned = integ.godaddy.is_owned(domain)
    price = 0.0
    if not owned:
        quote = integ.availability.check([domain])[0]
        if not quote.available or quote.price_usd is None:
            raise PlanError(f"Sorry, {domain} is no longer available. Please pick another name.")
        price = float(quote.price_usd)

    current = integ.godaddy.get_records(domain) if owned else []
    mailbox = f"orders@{domain}"
    other_txt = [{"data": r["data"]} for r in current
                 if r["type"] == "TXT" and r["name"] == "@" and not r["data"].lower().startswith("v=spf1")]
    changes = [
        change(domain, "A", "@", current, [{"data": settings.server_ip}], f"Point {domain} to your website"),
        change(domain, "MX", "@", current, [{"data": host, "priority": prio} for prio, host in TITAN_MX],
               f"Deliver email for {domain} to your mailbox"),
        change(domain, "TXT", "@", current, other_txt + [{"data": TITAN_SPF}],
               "Allow your mailbox to send email for you (so it doesn't land in spam)"),
        change(domain, "TXT", "titan1._domainkey", current, [{"data": DKIM_PENDING}],
               "Sign your emails so customers can trust they're from you", deferred=True),
        change(domain, "TXT", "_dmarc", current, [{"data": DMARC}],
"""FastAPI app: API routers, internal endpoints, seller sites and the built frontend.

Requests whose Host is a seller site (`<subdomain>.APP_DOMAIN` or a seller's
own domain in the DB) get that seller's pages; everything else gets the app.
"""

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path

from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, HTMLResponse, PlainTextResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from sqlmodel import Session

from app.config import REPO_ROOT, Settings, get_settings
from app.db import get_session, init_db
from app.routers import businesses, contact, health, internal, launch, report
from app.sites import routes as seller_routes

FRONTEND_DIST = REPO_ROOT / "frontend" / "dist"
REPLAY_PAGE = REPO_ROOT / "replay" / "build.html"  # built by scripts/build-replay.sh, served at /build

BUILD_COMING_SOON = """<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>How LaunchWitness was built</title>
<body style="font-family:system-ui;max-width:560px;margin:15vh auto;padding:0 16px;color:#1f2937;line-height:1.5">
<h1>How this was built: coming soon</h1>
<p>LaunchWitness was built in a series of sessions with Claude Code. The full replay of those sessions will appear
on this page shortly.</p><p><a href="/">← Back to LaunchWitness</a></p></body>"""


def start_monitor(settings: Settings):
    """Light monitoring (SPEC §7). Off with MONITOR_ENABLED=false; tests never run this."""
    from app.agents.claude_client import make_claude_client
    from app.db import get_engine
    from app.integrations import for_business, get_integrations, get_practice_integrations
    from app.monitor.scheduler import Monitor

    engine = get_engine()
    claude = make_claude_client(settings, engine if settings.claude_mode == "live" else None)
    monitor = Monitor(engine, settings, lambda b: for_business(b, get_integrations(), get_practice_integrations()),
                      claude)
    monitor.start()
    return monitor


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI):
    init_db()
    settings = get_settings()
    monitor = start_monitor(settings) if settings.monitor_enabled else None
    yield
    if monitor is not None:
        monitor.shutdown()


def create_app(*, frontend_dist: Path = FRONTEND_DIST, replay_page: Path = REPLAY_PAGE,
               run_lifespan: bool = True) -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(title="LaunchWitness", lifespan=lifespan if run_lifespan else None)
    app.include_router(health.router)
    app.include_router(internal.router)
    app.include_router(businesses.router)
    app.include_router(launch.router)
    app.include_router(report.router)
    app.include_router(contact.router)
    app.include_router(seller_routes.router)

    assets = frontend_dist / "assets"
    if assets.is_dir():
        app.mount("/assets", StaticFiles(directory=assets), name="assets")

    @app.get("/{path:path}", include_in_schema=False)
    def frontend(
        path: str,
        request: Request,
        settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)],
        session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)],
    ):
        if path.startswith(("api/", "internal/")):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404)
        page = seller_routes.seller_page(path, request, settings, session)
        if page is not None:
            return page
        if path.rstrip("/") == "build":
            if replay_page.is_file():
                return FileResponse(replay_page, media_type="text/html")
            return HTMLResponse(BUILD_COMING_SOON)
        index = frontend_dist / "index.html"
        if not index.is_file():
            return PlainTextResponse("Frontend not built. Run: cd frontend && npm run build")
        return FileResponse(index)

    return app


app = create_app()

# Environment update
 - Primary working directory: c:\Users\Aarushi\Downloads\LaunchWitness\backend\app (was c:\Users\Aarushi\Downloads\LaunchWitness)

# Phase 0 report

## Verification
- **Tests:** 339 passed, 2 skipped (real infrastructure). **Frontend build:** clean.
- **GoDaddy prod API:** HTTP 200, one domain, `launchwitness.com` ACTIVE. Per-shop A records through the API are possible. This proves read access only; the first record write gets verified on Wednesday, with a hand-made wildcard as the fallback.
- **`docs/AUDIT_2026-11-15.md` does not exist** in the repo on any branch. I checked the B/S items in your prompt against the code instead. Please add the file if you have it.
- **I don't have the build-phase evaluation criteria** from the kickoff webinar. Paste them if you can; they could reorder everything below.

## Verdict
The execution is strong, but the idea as it stands is a website builder with a self-test. I'd shortlist it for the Top 10 on execution if the live demo works; I would not put it in the Top 3 yet.

What a skeptical GoDaddy judge says in the first 30 seconds:
1. **"You're testing your own code."** The proof only covers shops LaunchWitness built and hosts, which is a health check. The pitch says "Airo builds, LaunchWitness proves", but it cannot check an Airo site. This is the biggest hole.
2. **"Where's the agent?"** Claude makes three single-shot calls. The Doctor picks one of five options, which is a classifier. The one phase that fixes this (Phase 5) is last and optional.
3. **"Where's GoDaddy?"** With subdomains only and manual purchases, real GoDaddy API use is close to zero unless each launch writes its own DNS record.
4. **"Indian home sellers live on WhatsApp."** An order emailed to an inbox she rarely opens is a weak pipeline.

On your direct questions:
- **Is the problem real?** Yes. Forms and order emails that fail silently are common, but mostly on sites people already have, not on shops we just built.
- **Positioning:** the reliability agent is stronger than the website generator, but only if points 1–3 are fixed. Keep "Is your shop actually ready for customers?" for sellers; "reliability and operations agent" is judge language only.
- **Is monitoring the differentiator?** Not as uptime pings, which are a commodity. A daily real test order with a hop trace and history is the differentiator.
- **What to monitor, by value:** daily test order, then certificate, then the shop's DNS answer, then mailbox plan expiry, then domain expiry. Broken-link checks add nothing on a fixed template.
- **Auto-fix or ask:** fix automatically only what we wrote and the owner already approved (re-point the address, retry the certificate, re-add our records). Restoring a backup or touching records we didn't write needs approval. Money is never automatic.
- **The killer feature:** break something live, and the trace shows which hop died; the Doctor investigates, fixes it and re-proves it, ending in a public receipt.

## Ranked changes
I'd make 1–5 even with the deadline.

1. **"Check any address" on the landing page.** Paste any domain and get read-only public checks (DNS, HTTPS, certificate days left, mail records) in plain English. It makes the pitch true for sites we didn't build and gives judges something to try on their own domain. About 3 hours, reusing checker code, with an SSRF guard.
2. **Promote the investigating Doctor above shop design.** It is the only real agent loop.
3. **Per-shop A records through the GoDaddy API, no wildcard.** This gives real DNS backup, write and authoritative verification per launch, and a safe fault to stage (delete one shop's record). Add a hard guard: on the app zone, code may only write A records for shop slugs, never `@`, `*` or mail records.
4. **One real seller.** Get one actual home seller launched by Thursday, with their own "Yes, I got it" tap in the report. This needs no code and carries the most weight at an inclusive-innovation event.
5. **Keep one WhatsApp link** on the order confirmation page ("Send this order to the shop"). It is about 30 lines and answers objection 4. The rest of the WhatsApp work stays cut.
6. **Minimal bounce check:** look for a bounce carrying the nonce in `hello@`. Only if time allows.

## The audit items
Confirmed in code: B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B8, B9, S7. I did not check B7 or S6. I could not find phone numbers in audit details (S8), so I'll add a test that locks that in.

Missing from the list:
- **Certificate rate limit.** Let's Encrypt allows about 50 new certificates a week per domain, and every shop subdomain uses one. Live shops need a cap; this also justifies admin approval.
- **One mailbox carries everything.** Sign-in links, order emails and alerts all go through `hello@`. It has a daily send limit (I need to verify the number) and expires around Dec 15, four days after the finale.
- **B4 shrinks if own-domain launches stay practice-only.** Mail-record checks become read-only on the sending domain and nothing writes mail records for real.

## Decisions
I agree with 1–5. Changes I'd argue for:
- **Own-domain launch:** cut it outright, not stretch. Say "subdomains only" in the product.
- **Claim flow:** nothing is deployed, so no owner-link shops exist. Fold it into "guest practice, then sign in to keep it" as one mechanism.
- **Three themes:** one template with three palettes. A prettier shop makes us look more like a builder; design effort goes to the trace and report page.

<ide_selection>The user selected the lines 1 to 274 from c:\Users\Aarushi\Downloads\LaunchWitness\docs\SPEC.md:
# LaunchWitness — Final Build Spec

As of 2026-11-14 · GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026 (HackerEarth) · Round 2 build Nov 13–20 · submit by Nov 20 · Top 10 announced Nov 30 · onsite finale Pune, Dec 11.

LaunchWitness is a working name.

---

## 1. Pitch

**One line for judges:** "Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy and proves everything works before your first customer arrives."

LaunchWitness takes a small seller from a few lines of description to a live business on her own domain: website, business email, and an order form that reaches her inbox. Then it checks every part for real, fixes or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps checking lightly afterwards.

**What makes it different.** Most AI builders stop at "your site is ready." LaunchWitness shows the proof: a real test order arriving in her inbox, every check green, and a report with the time each one passed. The safety rules (approve before spending, preview before changing, undo on failure) are what let an AI be trusted to spend money and change settings for a non-technical owner.

**Why it fits GoDaddy.** Small businesses buying a domain, a website and an email is GoDaddy's core business. LaunchWitness uses GoDaddy's Domains, DNS and Email as the engine, not decoration. GoDaddy's own AI tools already help people get online; LaunchWitness adds the missing piece: proof that it all works, before customers find out it doesn't.

---

## 2. Problem and the story

Small sellers either never get their own online presence, or they get one that is quietly broken.

1. **They don't start, because setup is technical.** A GoDaddy survey found 63% of India's small businesses had no website; of those planning one, only 15% owned a domain, and 30% wanted someone to build and manage it for them (DNA India). The survey is several years old: present it as background, not today's figure.
2. **When they do start, it's often half-working.** A March 2026 analysis put DMARC adoption at 44.9% for small businesses vs 75.3% for large enterprises (Cross-Sector DNS & Email Security). A scan of 200 small and mid-size business domains found 36% missing SPF and over two-thirds with no DMARC record (DEV). Result: order emails land in spam, and the owner never knows — she just thinks business is slow.
3. **AI could do the setup, but isn't trusted to.** Buying a domain and changing settings means spending money and risking email. An owner who can't read a DNS record can't check an agent's work.

Open question: find one current (2025–26) India-specific figure on small businesses without websites before the deck.

**Demo persona: Meera.** Meera sells custom cakes from home and takes orders over Instagram DMs. No website, no business email, never touched DNS. She types two lines and pastes her price list. A few minutes later she has meerabakes.in with her real menu and prices, hello@meerabakes.in, and an order form that lands in that inbox. Before she shares the link with a single customer, LaunchWitness places a test order, watches it arrive, and shows her: **"Your business is ready for customers."**

---

## 3. How it works (user flow)

Seven steps from description to proof; Meera does four of them, and only one costs money.

1. **Describe.** A few lines + price list (typed, pasted or photo). No WhatsApp/Instagram API.
   - Claude (one call) returns the business profile (name, products, prices, hours, area, tone) **plus** the site copy (tagline, about, item descriptions) **plus** how customers order: selling point, days of notice, pickup / delivery and delivery charge, whether customers may add a message for an item, the name the seller's UPI app shows, and her food licence (FSSAI) number if given. Plain code then tidies the reply (delivery is never a menu item; extras such as toppers are marked as extras; ordering rules leave the hours line).
   - **Scope guard (v1 = sellers who take orders).** If the business needs bookings rather than orders (salon, tuition, clinic, classes), the Reader says so in one plain sentence and no shop is built.
2. **Review.** She sees the profile as a form and fixes anything wrong. No AI.
3. **Pick a name.** Claude (one small call) suggests ~10 domain names; code checks real availability + price; shows the best 3.
4. **Preview and approve.** Code fills the ONE fixed template, the same for every seller (no per-business code or CSS; category colours come from a fixed palette by position): header with short badges taken only from her data, menu with prices and an Add button per item (a basket that also works without JavaScript; long menus get two columns and a search box), extras listed apart, about, hours, pickup/delivery, "Order on WhatsApp" link (`wa.me`), UPI QR with "Your UPI app should show: <name>", optional FSSAI number in the footer, privacy page. No "Verified" label anywhere. One approval card lists the domain, total cost and every setting to be made. **Nothing is bought or changed until she taps Approve.**
5. **Launch.** Code only: back up DNS, buy the domain (or use a free sandbox subdomain), point it at the server, set up email, put the site live with HTTPS. Each step streams on screen.
6. **Launch check.** Code checks the site opens, HTTPS is valid, email settings are correct, then places a real test order through her form. If anything fails, the Doctor explains it in one sentence, applies a safe fix or undoes the change, and re-checks until green.
7. **Report and watch.** Report headed **"Your business is ready for customers"**: every check, result, time passed. After launch, the same checks re-run lightly on a timer and alert her if something breaks.

**Two launch modes, same code:**
- **Sandbox launch** at `<slug>.<APP_DOMAIN>`: free, real DNS writes on the app's own domain, real checks. Used for development, rehearsals and judges trying it.
- **Full launch** on a purchased domain: run once, for the recorded demo.

---

## 4. Features

Eight core features first; no stretch item starts until all eight run end to end.

| # | Feature | Tier | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Business reader | Core | Description + price list (text or photo) → editable profile + site copy, one Claude call |
| 2 | Name finder | Core | Claude suggests names; code checks real availability and price; shows 3 |
| 3 | Site builder | Core | One fixed template for every seller: badges from data, menu + basket, extras, about, hours, pickup/delivery, order form, WhatsApp link, UPI QR, privacy page |
| 3a | Orders and payment (session 9) | Core | Order date (min notice enforced), pickup/delivery, quantities, totals worked out on the server; per-order UPI pay link + QR (no gateway, no money passes through us); order ID + status page (Received → Confirmed → Paid → Preparing → Ready / Out for delivery → Delivered / Picked up, or Cancelled); seller's order list on her private link; WhatsApp hand-offs via `wa.me` links |
| 3b | Trust and safety (session 9) | Core | Verify the owner's email before any real launch; Claude policy check that can only hold a shop for team review (never launches); "Report this shop" link + admin pause switch |
| 4 | Launch engine | Core | Plan → preview of changes → approval card → execute (GoDaddy Domains, DNS, Email); sandbox + full modes |
| 5 | Launch check | Core | Site resolves, HTTPS valid, email settings present, real test order arrives |
| 6 | Repair during launch | Core | Doctor explains a failed check, applies a playbook fix or undoes from backup, re-checks |
| 7 | Launch report | Core | One page per business: every check, result, timestamp, plus audit log |
| 8 | Light monitoring | Core (light) | Timer re-checks, domain/cert expiry warnings, alert to personal email, "Run checks now" |
| 9 | Full monitoring | Stretch | Daily test order, change detection ("Was this you?"), incident history |
| 10 | /verify page | Stretch | Official Instagram/WhatsApp listed, backed by a DNS TXT record, so buyers spot fakes |
| 11 | MCP server | Stretch | Engine tools over MCP behind the same safety gates |
| 12 | Fleet view | Stretch | Dashboard of all launched businesses |

Out of scope: payment gateways or holding money (UPI pay links only; "Connect Razorpay (after seller KYC)" is future work), appointments/booking, inventory, SMS, WhatsApp Business / Instagram APIs, multiple templates, custom code generation.

---

## 5. Agents

Claude decides and explains; plain code acts and checks. Three steps use Claude; nothing that spends money or changes settings is left to the model alone.

| Agent | Job | Claude or code | Model | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reader | Profile + site copy + ordering details from text or photo; orders vs bookings | Claude, 1 call | Strong (vision + structured output) | Profile JSON + copy (code tidies it) |
| Policy check (session 9) | Is this shop OK to put live? | Claude decides, code holds | Cheap | OK, or "hold for review" + one plain reason; it can never launch or unpause |
| Namer | Suggest names; check availability + price | Claude suggests, code checks | Cheap | 3 available domains with prices |
| Planner | Every action, setting and cost | Code, fixed schema | — | Plan + before/after preview |
| Executor | Run the approved plan step by step, backup first | Code only | — | Step log |
| Checker | Live checks | Code only | — | Pass/fail per check |
| Doctor | Explain a failed check in one sentence; pick a fix | Claude chooses, code applies | Cheap | Fix + re-check result |

A manager loop runs them in order and stops at the approval card. **Doctor playbook (fixed, in code):** undo from backup · re-add MX · re-add SPF/DKIM/DMARC · retry certificate · re-point site address. It cannot write arbitrary settings.

Cost shape: ~3 Claude calls per launch + 1 per failed check.

---

## 6. Launch checks and repair

Repair happens during launch, because that's where setups actually go wrong: settings not spread yet, a certificate failing first time, a mailbox not ready, an email setting missing, a step failing halfway.

| Check | How | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Domain points to the site | DNS lookup against GoDaddy's authoritative nameservers (not a cached resolver) | Re-point, wait, re-check |
| Site opens over HTTPS | Fetch, validate certificate | Retry certificate, re-check |
| Email settings correct | Look up MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Re-add the missing record from the plan |
| Test order arrives | Submit the real form; email carries a "Yes, I got it" link | Check mailbox readiness + MX, retry |
| Launch finished cleanly | Step log shows every step done | Resume the failed step, or undo DNS from backup |

**Repair rules:** max 3 attempts per check, then stop and explain in plain words. Repair never spends money. Every attempt goes to the audit log.

**Confirming the test order:** for real sellers the app can't read their inbox (GoDaddy emails mailbox passwords to the account owner only), so the seller taps "Yes, I got it". For the demo mailbox, the checker can also read the inbox over IMAP (password in env).

**Demo failure:** during launch one check fails on purpose (e.g. DMARC missing → orders would land in spam). The Doctor explains, re-adds, re-checks to green. The fault is staged — say so if asked.

---

## 7. Monitoring after launch

Light monitoring is core; full only if time permits. It re-runs launch checks on a timer (GoDaddy's API has no webhooks).

**Light (build now)**

| How often | What |
|---|---|
| Every 15 minutes | Site opens, HTTPS valid |
| Daily | DNS + email settings still match launch; days left on certificate and domain |

- On failure: re-check once a minute later (rule out blips), then Doctor explains + safe playbook fix.
- Anything needing money or her action (renewal, payment): alert only, at 30 / 7 / 1 days before expiry.
- Alerts go to her **personal email**, not the business inbox.
- "Run checks now" button = same checks on demand (this is how the demo shows it).

**Full (if time permits):** daily real test order; change detection ("Was this you? Tap to restore") instead of silent undo; incident history on the report.

**Honest framing:** in the demo everything sits in the app's GoDaddy account, so little can break after launch. Monitoring matters most once it runs on her own account. Pitch it as insurance, not the hero.

---

## 8. Architecture and GoDaddy usage

One GoDaddy Docker VPS (4 vCPU / 8 GB, provided at $0) runs everything; GoDaddy and Claude are called as APIs.

- **Caddy:** HTTPS for the app and every seller site; on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint that only approves domains in the DB.
- **FastAPI:** agents, API, monitoring scheduler, and every seller site (served by `Host` header from one template + profile).
- **React (Vite):** seller-facing app, built and served as static files.
- **SQLite:** profiles, plans, DNS backups, check results, audit log.
- **Outside:** Claude API; GoDaddy Domains/DNS/Email (OTE sandbox in dev, `GODADDY_ENV=ote|prod`); SMTP through the app's one mailbox.
- **Secrets** live only in environment variables.
- **Sandbox subdomains** need a wildcard `*.<APP_DOMAIN>` A record → VPS.

| Step | GoDaddy piece | Calls |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Domains API (or `gddy`) | availability, suggestions, price quote |
| Buy | godaddy.com checkout with credit (demo); Domains API purchase only behind guards | purchase after approval |
| Point | DNS API | list records (backup), set A, MX, SPF/DKIM/DMARC |
| Mailbox | Titan email via `gddy` / Email API | create mailbox, poll until ready |
| Host | Docker VPS | A record → VPS; Caddy issues HTTPS |
| Undo | DNS API | write backup back |

**Access limits:** production Availability API needs 50+ domains or ~$20/month spend; DNS API needs ≥1 domain. So: buy the app domain first; check availability via `gddy`, OTE, or free RDAP if production stays blocked.

Say plainly to judges: hosting is the Docker VPS, not GoDaddy's Hosting API.

---

## 9. Safety rules

1. **Approve before spending.** Purchase/mailbox only after Approve on a card showing exact cost.
2. **Preview before changing.** Every DNS change shown as a before/after diff first.
3. **Back up, then undo.** Before any DNS write, save current records as JSON. Failed launch check can write the backup back. Failed mailbox step is retried, not undone.
4. **Scoped actions.** Each launch touches only its own domain. Doctor picks from a fixed playbook; anything else is refused and logged.
5. **Spend guards in code.** `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false` default, hard `MAX_SPEND_USD` cap, purchase only when flag on AND owner approved.

Every step goes to the audit log shown in the report.

---

## 10. Budget

**GoDaddy:** VPS is added to the cart at $0 by organizers. ~$25 in-store credit covers domain + email. Buy on godaddy.com only after organizers confirm credit; use the CLI to explore and manage.

| Item | Paid by | Expected cost | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 vCPU / 8 GB Docker VPS | Organizers ($0 in cart) | $0 | Check out after confirmation |
| App domain | Credit | Cart price; compare with `gddy` | Buy first (unlocks DNS) |
| Titan Pro Light, 1-month term, 1 mailbox | Credit | ~$2–5 | Buy after domain; create hello@ with `gddy` |
| Meera's demo domain | Credit, if room | Cart price | One full launch for the recording |
| Meera's own mailbox | Credit, if room | Another Pro Light month | Likely skip; test orders go to app mailbox (say so) |

If money runs out: skip Meera's domain; full launch on a subdomain; show purchase in dry-run. SMTP tip: if login fails use `smtpout.secureserver.net` with the full address as username.

**Claude: $100, API only, for the product.** None of it for Claude Code.
- ~3 small calls per launch (cents).
- Strong model only for Reader; cheap for Namer + Doctor.
- Dev: saved fixtures, not live calls, for UI work.
- Live link: per-visitor limit, max-token cap per call, daily spend cap.
- Check spend in the Claude console daily.

---

## 11. Submission (HackerEarth, by Nov 20)

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Title | LaunchWitness: from description to a proven, live business |
| Description | Demo video link (YouTube, unlisted) first line, then project brief + link to the build replay page |
| Theme | Open Innovation |
| Demo Link | Live app URL on the app domain, with a free sandbox launch judges can try |
| Repository URL | GitHub repo |
| Source Code | Zip of repo, no secrets |
| Additional File | Project brief PDF |

Build process for judges: one combined claude-replay page of all Claude Code sessions, hosted at `https://<APP_DOMAIN>/build`, plus `docs/BUILD_LOG.md`.

---

## 12. Demo video script (3 minutes, screen + voiceover, no face)

| Time | Scene | On screen | Voiceover |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Meera | Instagram: price list highlight, orders in DMs | "Meera has customers. She doesn't have a business online." |
| 0:20–0:45 | Describe | Two lines + price list; profile appears; fix one price | "She describes her business the way she'd tell a friend." |
| 0:45–1:05 | Name + approve | 3 domains with prices; approval card; tap Approve | "Nothing is bought until she says yes." |
| 1:05–1:30 | Launch | Step log streams; site live over HTTPS | "Her site, her domain, her email." |
| 1:30–2:15 | Proof + fix | Test order lands in inbox; one check fails (spam risk); Doctor sentence; fix; green | "Before her first customer, LaunchWitness checks everything, and fixes what's wrong." |
| 2:15–2:40 | Report | "Ready for customers" + timer + expiry warning | "And it keeps checking after launch." |
| 2:40–3:00 | Close | Logo + tagline | "Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy, and proves it works before your first customer arrives." |

Never buy a second domain on camera. Record a backup run. Rehearse proof + fix until boring.

---

## 13. Judge Q&A

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Doesn't GoDaddy already have AI for this? | GoDaddy's AI helps people get online. LaunchWitness proves it works (a real order in her inbox) and fixes what doesn't, before customers notice. |
| Who owns the domain? | Demo: my account. Real product: her own GoDaddy account, so she owns everything. |
| What can break after launch? | Not much in a setup we control. Real risks: renewal failing, someone changing settings while connecting another tool. Monitoring is insurance. |
| If her email breaks, how do you alert her? | Personal email, not the business inbox. |
| What if she changes a setting on purpose? | Not undone silently; it asks "Was this you?" first (full monitoring). Auto-fix only when a check fails. |
| What if your server goes down? | Checks stop too. Next step: outside uptime pinger. |
| Why trust AI with money and DNS? | It can't act alone: approval, preview, backup/undo, fixed fixes, spend caps in code. |
| Where does Claude matter? | Messy price list/photo → clean profile + copy; brand-fit names; plain-words diagnosis. Code acts. |
| Why VPS not GoDaddy Hosting? | Docker VPS option runs FastAPI + many seller sites with automatic HTTPS from one box. |
| Confirm delivery for real sellers? | "Yes, I got it" link in the test email; no mailbox password [REDACTED] |
| Was the demo failure real? | Staged so it shows reliably; detection and fix are real code. |
| Cost per seller? | A few Claude calls (cents) + domain + mailbox she'd buy anyway. |
| How does she get paid? | Each order shows "Pay ₹X via UPI": a prefilled UPI link on phones and a QR on laptops, with the order ID as the note. Money goes straight from the customer's UPI app to hers; it never passes through us. She marks the order Paid after checking her UPI app. Card payments ("Connect Razorpay") come later, after the seller's KYC. |
| How does the customer know what's happening? | A status page per order (unguessable ID, first name + items only), plus a ready-typed WhatsApp message the seller sends with one tap. No SMS, no WhatsApp Business API. |
| What if she never opens her business inbox? | New orders also go to her personal email, and the customer can send the order to her WhatsApp from the thank-you screen. |
| Can a scammer launch a fake shop? | The owner's email is verified before a real launch, a policy check can hold a shop for review, every shop has "Report this shop", and the team can pause it. |
| Can a salon or tutor use it? | Not yet: v1 is for sellers who take orders. The Reader says so plainly instead of building a half-working shop. |
| Who pays renewal next year? | The seller, to GoDaddy, on her own account. We warn her at 30 / 7 / 1 days. |

---

## 14. Risks and fallbacks

| Risk | Check by | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Credits not yet received | Office hours Nov 14 | Build locally against OTE + fakes |
| Domain + Pro Light cost more than credit | Cart, Nov 15 | Cheaper TLD; skip Meera's domain + mailbox |
| Production Availability/DNS API blocked | Nov 15 after app domain | `gddy`, OTE or RDAP; app domain unlocks DNS |
| Mailbox creation fails via CLI/API | Nov 15 | Create in dashboard; engine still sets settings + checks delivery |
| Settings/cert slow on camera | Nov 18 rehearsal | Query authoritative NS; record the full launch |
| Claude spend creeps up | Daily | Fixtures in dev, caps on live link |
| Others build the same launch flow | — | Lead with proof + fix |
| Scope creep | Daily | No stretch before core runs end to end |
| Live demo fails at Dec 11 finale | Dec 11 | Play recording, then Q&A on live app |


This may or may not be related to the current task.</ide_selection>
